# Internal Mass Calculations: CS Audience Seating Area - Gymnasium

**Report Date:** April 9, 2026
**Scope:** Audience Seating Area – Gymnasium Space Type
**Purpose:** Calculate OpenStudio InternalMass properties for thermal modeling

---

## CS Audience Seating Area - Gymnasium

### Space Characteristics

**Typical Occupancy:** 50–400 spectators (event-driven; near-zero between events)
**Floor Area:** 75–400 m² (bleacher section plus front access aisle and side circulation); reference area: **150 m²**
**Ceiling Height:** 6–10 m (clear-span gymnasium volume; the bleacher zone shares the open gymnasium air space with the playing floor; no suspended ceiling at the bleacher elevation)
**Function:** Spectator audience seating in a K-12 school or small college/municipal gymnasium. The space zone encompasses the deployed telescoping aluminum bleacher structure on one or both side walls of the gymnasium, the front-access circulation aisle at the base of the bleachers, and the perimeter aisles at the top and ends. The playing floor zone is modeled separately; locker rooms, corridors, and mechanical spaces are separate zones. The reference configuration models a single-wall, 4-row telescoping aluminum bleacher bank in a mid-size K-12 secondary school gymnasium supporting basketball, volleyball, wrestling, and multi-sport events.

**Key Features:**
- Telescoping/retractable aluminum bleacher system (dominant element — the entire seating assembly)
- Aluminum seat planks (extruded hollow-section; seat surface for each row)
- Aluminum footboard planks (foot-rest/walking surface at the base of each row)
- Aluminum riser panels (vertical kick-plate between adjacent rows; formed aluminum sheet)
- Aluminum longitudinal stringers (structural support beams running the full width of the section, parallel to seating rows)
- Aluminum cross members and diagonal bracing (perpendicular to seats, spanning the front-to-back depth of the bleacher structure)
- Aluminum end frames (structural uprights and horizontal ties at each end of the bleacher section)
- Steel safety guardrails (top rail, front base rail, and side-end rails at perimeter)
- No fixed upholstered seats (bleacher plank surface is bare anodized aluminum)
- No fixed aisle handrails integral to the seating rows (safety guardrails at perimeter only)
- No HVAC supply under-seat plenums (gymnasium HVAC serves the entire open volume from overhead units)

### Reference Configuration

**150 m² gymnasium bleacher zone:**
- 4-row telescoping aluminum bleacher section
- Section width: 13.8 m (30 seats per row × 0.46 m center-to-center seat spacing)
- Row pitch: 0.76 m (front-to-front); riser height: 0.305 m (12 in.); seat plank depth: 0.285 m
- Total deployed depth (4 rows): 4 × 0.76 = 3.04 m
- Total seats: 4 rows × 30 seats = **120 seats**
- Seating density: 120 / 150 = **0.80 seats/m²**
- Front access aisle: 1.2 m wide × 13.8 m (included in 150 m² zone)
- Perimeter circulation at top and ends: balance of reference area
- Safety guardrails: top (2 rails × 13.8 m), front base rail (13.8 m), side-end rails (2 × 1.5 m)

---

## Component Inventory

### 1. Aluminum Seat Planks (120 per 150 m²)

**Extruded Aluminum Bleacher Seat Plank (hollow-section extrusion, 6-inch nominal width):**
- Seat plank width per seat position: 0.46 m (center-to-center seat spacing)
- Seat surface exposed depth: 0.285 m (11.2 in. — horizontal surface available as seating area per row)
- Extrusion profile: hollow rectangular section, approximately 152 mm × 38 mm outer dimension, 3.2 mm wall; ribbed web interior
- Plank linear weight: 0.93 kg/m (standard commercial aluminum bleacher plank)
- Finish: mill finish anodized aluminum

**Surface Area per Seat:**

*Top (seating surface — fully exposed to room air):*
- 0.46 × 0.285 = **0.131 m²**

*Bottom (underside — partially exposed between structural stringers):*
- Exposure factor 0.70 (longitudinal stringers and cross members block approximately 30% of underside)
- 0.46 × 0.285 × 0.70 = **0.092 m²**

*Front and rear edges (extrusion thickness, 38 mm):*
- 2 × 0.46 × 0.038 = **0.035 m²** (includes forward overhang edge and back edge at riser base)

**Seat Plank SA per Seat: 0.131 + 0.092 + 0.035 = 0.258 m²**

**Mass per Seat:**
- 0.93 kg/m × 0.46 m = **0.428 kg**

**Per Floor Area (120 planks in 150 m²):**
- Surface Area: (120 × 0.258) / 150 = 30.96 / 150 = **0.206 m²/m²**
- Mass: (120 × 0.428) / 150 = 51.36 / 150 = **0.342 kg/m²**

---

### 2. Aluminum Footboard Planks (120 per 150 m²)

**Extruded Aluminum Footboard Plank (same extrusion profile as seat plank):**
- Each of the 4 rows has a dedicated footboard plank at the base of the row, providing the foot-rest surface for seated occupants and serving as the walking surface for access to upper rows
- Footboard width per seat position: 0.46 m; footboard depth: 0.285 m (identical extrusion to seat plank)
- Plank linear weight: 0.93 kg/m

**Surface Area per Seat:**

*Top (foot-rest/walking surface — fully exposed):*
- 0.46 × 0.285 = **0.131 m²**

*Bottom (underside — partially exposed between stringers):*
- 0.46 × 0.285 × 0.70 = **0.092 m²**

*Front and rear edges:*
- 2 × 0.46 × 0.038 = **0.035 m²**

**Footboard Plank SA per Seat: 0.258 m²**

**Mass per Seat: 0.93 × 0.46 = 0.428 kg**

**Per Floor Area (120 footboards in 150 m²):**
- Surface Area: (120 × 0.258) / 150 = **0.206 m²/m²**
- Mass: (120 × 0.428) / 150 = **0.342 kg/m²**

---

### 3. Aluminum Riser Panels (120 per 150 m²)

**Formed Aluminum Sheet Riser Panel:**
- Each of the 4 rows has a full-width riser panel at the vertical face between adjacent row levels
- Panel dimensions per seat position: 0.305 m height (riser height) × 0.46 m width × 0.002 m thickness (2 mm formed aluminum sheet)
- Finish: anodized aluminum

**Surface Area per Panel:**

*Front face (exposed to lower row — fully visible):*
- 0.305 × 0.46 = **0.140 m²**

*Rear face (exposed to upper row — 50% exposure; partially shadowed by seat plank above):*
- 0.305 × 0.46 × 0.50 = **0.070 m²**

*Top and bottom edges (2 mm thickness — negligible):*
- 2 × 0.46 × 0.002 = **0.002 m²**

**Riser Panel SA per Position: 0.140 + 0.070 + 0.002 = 0.212 m²**

**Mass per Panel:**
- 0.305 × 0.46 × 0.002 × 2,700 = **0.759 kg**

**Per Floor Area (120 panels in 150 m²):**
- Surface Area: (120 × 0.212) / 150 = 25.44 / 150 = **0.170 m²/m²**
- Mass: (120 × 0.759) / 150 = 91.08 / 150 = **0.607 kg/m²**

---

### 4. Aluminum Longitudinal Stringers (5 per section)

**Structural Aluminum Rectangular Hollow Section Stringer:**
- A 4-row bleacher system has 5 longitudinal stringers — one at each row transition level (base level, row 1, row 2, row 3, top of row 4)
- Each stringer runs the full width of the section: 13.8 m
- Profile: 76 mm × 51 mm × 2 mm rectangular hollow section aluminum
- Perimeter: 2 × (0.076 + 0.051) = **0.254 m**
- Cross-sectional wall area: 0.254 × 0.002 = **5.08 × 10⁻⁴ m²/m**
- Mass per meter: 5.08 × 10⁻⁴ × 2,700 = **1.37 kg/m**

**Per Stringer:**
- Mass: 1.37 × 13.8 = **18.91 kg**
- Exposed SA (exposure factor 0.60 — top face partially blocked by planks): 0.254 × 13.8 × 0.60 = **2.103 m²**

**Per Floor Area (5 stringers in 150 m²):**
- Total mass: 5 × 18.91 = 94.55 kg
- Surface Area: (5 × 2.103) / 150 = 10.52 / 150 = **0.070 m²/m²**
- Mass: 94.55 / 150 = **0.630 kg/m²**

---

### 5. Cross Members and Diagonal Bracing (per section)

**Aluminum Cross Members (7 per section, spaced at 2.0 m along 13.8 m width):**
- Each cross member spans the full deployed depth of the 4-row section: 3.04 m
- Profile: 51 mm × 51 mm × 2 mm square hollow aluminum
- Perimeter: 4 × 0.051 = **0.204 m**
- Mass/m: 0.204 × 0.002 × 2,700 = **1.10 kg/m**
- Mass per cross member: 1.10 × 3.04 = **3.34 kg**
- 7 cross members: 7 × 3.34 = **23.4 kg**

**Aluminum Diagonal Bracing (28 diagonals — 4 tiers × 7 frames):**
- One diagonal per tier per transverse frame, bracing each row-height panel
- Diagonal length per tier (row pitch 0.76 m, riser height 0.305 m): √(0.76² + 0.305²) = √(0.578 + 0.093) = **0.819 m**
- Same profile as cross members: 1.10 kg/m
- Mass per diagonal: 1.10 × 0.819 = **0.901 kg**
- 28 diagonals: 28 × 0.901 = **25.2 kg**

**Total Component 5 Mass: 23.4 + 25.2 = 48.6 kg**

**SA (exposure factor 0.50 — bracing elements are largely interior to the structure):**
- Cross members: 7 × 0.204 × 3.04 × 0.50 = **2.17 m²**
- Diagonals: 28 × 0.204 × 0.819 × 0.50 = **2.34 m²**
- Total SA: 4.51 m²

**Per Floor Area (in 150 m²):**
- Surface Area: 4.51 / 150 = **0.030 m²/m²**
- Mass: 48.6 / 150 = **0.324 kg/m²**

---

### 6. Aluminum End Frames (2 per section)

**Structural End Frame Assembly at Each End of the Bleacher Section:**
- 2 end frames per section, one at each end of the 13.8 m bleacher bank
- Each frame consists of 5 upright members (at each stringer level) and 4 horizontal tie members (spanning the 0.46 m depth of the end seat position)
- Upright profile: 76 mm × 76 mm × 3 mm square hollow aluminum; average height 0.90 m per upright
- Horizontal tie profile: 51 mm × 51 mm × 2 mm square hollow aluminum; 0.46 m per member

**Mass per End Frame:**
- Upright perimeter: 4 × 0.076 = 0.304 m; wall area: 0.304 × 0.003 = 9.12 × 10⁻⁴ m²/m; mass/m = 2.46 kg/m
- 5 uprights × 0.90 m × 2.46 = **11.1 kg**
- 4 horizontal ties × 0.46 m × 1.10 kg/m = **2.0 kg**
- Total per frame: **13.1 kg** (including fasteners and brackets: **~13.4 kg**)

**SA per End Frame (exposure factor 0.40 — largely at ends, partially shielded):**
- Uprights: 5 × 0.304 × 0.90 × 0.40 = **0.547 m²**
- Horizontal ties: 4 × 0.204 × 0.46 × 0.50 = **0.188 m²**
- Total per frame: **0.735 m²**

**Per Floor Area (2 frames in 150 m²):**
- Total mass: 2 × 13.4 = 26.8 kg
- Total SA: 2 × 0.735 = 1.47 m²
- Surface Area: 1.47 / 150 = **0.010 m²/m²**
- Mass: 26.8 / 150 = **0.179 kg/m²**

---

### 7. Steel Safety Guardrails (per section)

**Galvanized Steel Pipe Guardrail System:**
- Top rails: 2 rails × 13.8 m = 27.6 m (at top of row 4 and mid-height safety rail)
- Front base rail: 13.8 m (at the base of the bleacher front face)
- Side-end rails: 2 × 1.5 m = 3.0 m (at each end of the section)
- Total rail length: **44.4 m**
- Profile: 1.0 in. nominal thin-wall steel tube (OD = 25.4 mm); mass/m: **0.967 kg/m**

**Per Floor Area (44.4 m of rail in 150 m²):**
- SA: 44.4 × π × 0.0254 = 44.4 × 0.0798 = 3.54 m² → 3.54 / 150 = **0.024 m²/m²**
- Mass: 44.4 × 0.967 = 42.9 kg → 42.9 / 150 = **0.286 kg/m²**

## Composite Material Properties

### Mass-Weighted Material Property Derivation

**Material Fractions (by mass):**
- Aluminum alloy (seat planks, footboards, risers, stringers, cross members, end frames):
  - Mass = 2.710 − 0.286 = 2.424 kg/m²
  - Fraction: 2.424 / 2.710 = **0.894 (89.4%)**
- Galvanized steel (guardrails):
  - Mass = 0.286 kg/m²
  - Fraction: 0.286 / 2.710 = **0.106 (10.6%)**

**Material Properties:**

| Property | Aluminum Alloy | Galvanized Steel |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Density (kg/m³) | 2,700 | 7,850 |
| Specific Heat (J/kg·K) | 897 | 460 |
| Conductivity (W/m·K) | 205 | 50 |
| Thermal Absorptance | 0.90 | 0.90 |
| Solar Absorptance | 0.65 | 0.65 |

**Mass-Weighted Composite Properties (true physical values):**
- Specific Heat: 0.894 × 897 + 0.106 × 460 = 801.8 + 48.8 = **850.6 J/kg·K → 851 J/kg·K**
- Conductivity (true): 0.894 × 205 + 0.106 × 50 = 183.3 + 5.3 = **188.6 W/m·K**

**EnergyPlus Minimum Thickness Constraint:**

The true equivalent uniform slab thickness is:
```
t_true = Total Mass / (SA Ratio × ρ_mix_volume)
```

A volume-weighted density calculation is impractical for this structure (thin-wall hollow extrusions spanning a largely air-filled volume); the assembly is not a dense slab but a structural framework. The true equivalent physical thickness is far below EnergyPlus's practical minimum (3 mm). Using the minimum slab thickness of **10 mm** and solving for adjusted density to preserve the correct total mass per floor area:

```
ρ_adj = Total Mass / (SA Ratio × t_min)
      = 2.71 / (0.71 × 0.010)
      = 2.71 / 0.0071
      = 381.7 kg/m³  →  382 kg/m³
```

**EnergyPlus Conductivity Adjustment:**

The true composite conductivity (188.6 W/m·K) exceeds EnergyPlus's practical upper bound for stable internal surface calculations. Conductivity is capped at **50.0 W/m·K**, consistent with the Exercise Center bleacher treatment. This produces negligible modeling error: aluminum bleacher elements equilibrate with zone air temperature nearly instantaneously regardless of whether conductivity is modeled at 50 or 205 W/m·K; the thermal lag of any aluminum extrusion at this scale is measured in seconds.

### Final EnergyPlus Material Parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Name | Mixed_AudienceSeating_Gymnasium_10mm |
| Roughness | Smooth |
| Thickness (m) | 0.0100 |
| Conductivity (W/m·K) | 50.0 (adjusted; true: 188.6) |
| Density (kg/m³) | 382 (adjusted for 10 mm minimum thickness) |
| Specific Heat (J/kg·K) | 851 |
| Thermal Absorptance | 0.90 |
| Solar Absorptance | 0.65 |
| Visible Absorptance | 0.65 |

> Thermal absorptance set to 0.90 (standard for anodized aluminum surfaces and galvanized steel guardrails, both of which have moderate-to-high emissivity in the infrared range despite their reflective appearance in visible light). Solar and visible absorptance set to 0.65, reflecting the mid-silver anodized finish typical of gymnasium bleacher systems — slightly higher absorptance than bright polished aluminum, accounting for the matte anodized surface texture and accumulated surface aging in active gymnasium environments.

**Verification:**
```
Thermal Mass = SA ratio × Thickness × Density
             = 0.71 × 0.0100 × 382
             = 2.71 kg/m²  ✓  (matches component total of 2.710 kg/m²; <0.1% variance)

Thermal Capacitance = ρ × c_p
                    = 382 × 851
                    = 325,082 J/m³·K  ✓
```


## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Smaller-Scale All-Metal Assembly — Closely Related to Exercise Center Bleacher:**
- Low SA ratio (0.71 m²/m²) — the gymnasium bleacher's 4-row, 0.80 seats/m² configuration produces a lower SA ratio than the 6-row exercise center bleacher (1.03 m²/m²); the fewer rows and lower seat density reduce both the plank surface area contribution and the extent of structural framing, yielding the lowest SA ratio of the aluminum bleacher seating types
- Very low total thermal mass (2.71 kg/m²) — the lightest of all audience seating space types; the 4-row gymnasium bleacher is the minimum-complexity retractable seating system used in commercial/institutional buildings; mass reflects the deliberately lightweight aluminum construction required for retractability and daily deployment cycles
- Very high true conductivity (188.6 W/m·K) — essentially identical to the exercise center bleacher; the all-aluminum-dominant assembly equilibrates with zone air temperature nearly instantaneously; capped at 50.0 W/m·K for EnergyPlus numerical stability without affecting simulation accuracy
- EnergyPlus adjusted density (382 kg/m³) is slightly higher than the exercise center (332 kg/m³), reflecting the different SA ratio used for the density back-calculation — both represent the same physical material; the density adjustment is an artifact of the equivalent slab model, not a real compositional difference

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Very low total thermal energy storage (2.71 × 851 = 2,306 J/m²·K per floor area) — the gymnasium bleacher zone has negligible thermal flywheel capacity; the zone air temperature and bleacher surface temperature are essentially coupled; this is appropriate behavior for a system that is structurally designed to be as light as possible
- The aluminum plank system equilibrates essentially instantaneously with zone air changes — thermal lag of a single plank (effective resistance ≈ t/λ = 0.038/205 ≈ 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ m²·K/W) is negligible; pre-event conditioning need not account for any "warm-up" of the bleacher thermal mass
- The guardrails (steel, 0.286 kg/m²) contribute 10.6% of total mass from only 10.6% of the material fraction — their thin-wall hollow geometry provides significant convective exchange area at the perimeter aisle and top-of-bleacher elevation; they act as fin-like surfaces that exchange heat directly with the gymnasium air circulation

### Design Appropriateness

**School Gymnasium Bleacher Seating — Distinctive Thermal Profile:**
- **4-row retractable aluminum bleachers are the archetypal seating system for K-12 gymnasium audience areas** — school gymnasiums serving double-duty as event venues (basketball games, assemblies, performances) use the minimum seating row count needed to accommodate parent/community audiences; the 4-row configuration (120 seats at 0.80 seats/m²) is typical for secondary school gymnasiums seating 50–200 spectators
- **Lower seating density than exercise center** (0.80 vs 1.20 seats/m²) — the gymnasium bleacher zone includes proportionally more access aisle and perimeter circulation area relative to the seating rows; school gymnasium bleachers are typically accessed from the gymnasium floor during event transitions, requiring wider base aisles relative to the bleacher section size
- **The plank system (seat + footboard + riser) contributes 82.0% of SA but only 47.7% of mass** — the structural underframe (stringers, cross members, end frames) contributes 49.6% of total mass but only 15.5% of SA; the underframe is thermally significant by mass but largely concealed from direct room-air contact by the plank system above it
- **No soft furnishings in any form** — identical to the exercise center bleacher; the gymnasium audience seating zone is entirely aluminum and steel, with no polyurethane foam, commercial fabric, hardwood, ceramic, or organic material; the absence of soft furnishings confirms the extremely low thermal storage and near-instantaneous thermal response of this space type

### Comparison to Related Audience Seating Space Types

| Parameter | Gymnasium Bleacher | Exercise Center Bleacher | Auditorium Seating |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| SA Ratio (m²/m²) | 0.71 | 1.03 | 2.11 |
| Mass (kg/m²) | 2.71 | 3.42 | 15.36 |
| EnergyPlus Density (kg/m³) | 382 | 332 | 219 |
| Conductivity (W/m·K) | 50.0 (adj.) | 50.0 (adj.) | 0.966 |
| Specific Heat (J/kg·K) | 851 | 863 | 859 |
| Thermal Capacitance (J/m³·K) | 325,082 | 286,516 | 188,121 |
| Seats/m² | 0.80 | 1.20 | 1.50 |
| Rows | 4 | 6 | — |
| Dominant material | Aluminum | Aluminum | PU foam |
| EnergyPlus min. thickness required | Yes (10 mm) | Yes (10 mm) | No (33 mm natural) |

> The gymnasium bleacher represents a smaller, lower-density application of the same aluminum telescoping technology as the exercise center — the compositional profile (aluminum dominant, small steel guardrail contribution), material properties, and thermal behavior are essentially identical; the difference is purely one of scale. Both contrast sharply with the auditorium fixed theater seat: the auditorium achieves a 5.7× higher total thermal mass (15.36 vs 2.71 kg/m²) through the high polyurethane foam volume and complex multi-surface geometry of the upholstered seat, despite a lower true composite density. The gymnasium bleacher's adjusted EnergyPlus density (382 kg/m³) appears higher than both comparators, but this is a modeling artifact of the lower SA ratio used in the density back-calculation — the real material density (2,700 kg/m³ for aluminum) is the same in all aluminum bleacher systems.

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Gymnasium bleacher zones share the open air volume of the gymnasium with the playing floor zone; in most K-12 school energy models, the gymnasium is modeled as a single open zone (playing floor + bleacher seating combined) rather than separate thermal zones; if separate zoning is used, the bleacher zone's internal mass is negligible relative to the zone air volume
- High latent loads during events: 120 spectators (sedentary) × ~75 W sensible + 55 W latent = 9.0 kW sensible + 6.6 kW latent in 150 m²; these transient occupancy loads dominate the zone energy balance during events; the bleacher thermal mass is not a significant moderating factor
- The bleacher assembly provides negligible thermal lag — HVAC pre-conditioning of the gymnasium need not account for warming the bleacher internal mass; only the air volume and the gymnasium's structural thermal mass (concrete slab, masonry walls) require meaningful pre-conditioning time

**Operational Patterns:**
- School gymnasium schedule: typical after-school and evening events (basketball, volleyball, wrestling, assemblies); often 2–5 event days per week during active seasons; gymnasium is unoccupied and can be set back during school day and overnight
- Between events, the retracted or deployed bleacher structure exchanges heat freely with the gymnasium air volume; if retracted against the side wall between events, the exposed surface area is dramatically reduced
- For energy modeling, assume bleachers are deployed during the heating/cooling season (when school events occur); schedule the InternalMass using the space occupancy schedule

**Special Considerations:**
- **Retracted vs. deployed state**: when fully retracted, the 4-row bleacher collapses to a depth of approximately 0.3–0.5 m against the side wall; the exposed surface area is reduced to only the outer face of the stacked deck; EnergyPlus does not natively support variable InternalMass definitions, so the deployed condition is used as the design basis
- **Single-zone gymnasium modeling**: if the gymnasium is modeled as a single thermal zone (playing floor + bleacher), the internal mass from the bleacher zone should be included in the combined zone's InternalMass assignments; the playing area `InternalMassDefinition` for the combined zone should incorporate both the Gymnasium/Playing Area and Gymnasium Audience Seating contributions, scaled by their respective floor area fractions
- **Multi-wall bleacher configurations**: some gymnasiums have bleachers on both long walls; in this case the bleacher zone floor area and seat count are doubled, but the per-m² internal mass properties (SA ratio = 0.71, material definition) remain unchanged — the InternalMass object scales automatically with the zone floor area

---

*End of Calculation Report*

# Internal Mass Calculations: CS Audience Seating Area - Motion Picture Theater

**Report Date:** April 9, 2026
**Scope:** Audience Seating Area – Motion Picture Theater Space Type
**Purpose:** Calculate OpenStudio InternalMass properties for thermal modeling

---

## CS Audience Seating Area - Motion Picture Theater

### Space Characteristics

**Typical Occupancy:** 100–600 patrons (showtime-driven; near-zero between screenings)
**Floor Area:** 150–400 m² (seating deck only, excluding screen wall, projection booth, and lobby); reference area: **300 m²**
**Ceiling Height:** 5–10 m (sloped ceiling following stadium rake; acoustic treatment panels typically installed overhead)
**Function:** Fixed-seat audience seating in a commercial multiplex or single-screen cinema for projected motion picture presentations. The space is bounded by the seating deck proper: rows of fixed upholstered seats arranged on stepped concrete risers (stadium seating), cross aisles, perimeter aisles, and the side wall surfaces at the seat level. The screen, projection booth, concession areas, and lobby are modeled as separate zones. The reference configuration models a mid-size multiplex auditorium screen in a modern stadium-configuration cinema.

**Key Features:**
- Fixed upholstered cinema seats on stepped concrete risers (stadium configuration)
- Folding seat mechanism (spring-loaded, steel) with integrated armrest and cup holder
- ABS plastic cup holder insert (1 per seat; some configurations have 2 per armrest)
- Decorative plastic back-shell panel on seat back (visible to patron in row behind)
- Row end aisle standards (hollow square steel tube with powder-coat finish)
- Step transition handrails along center and side aisles (steel pipe)
- Acoustic ceiling panels and wall treatment (modeled as structural surfaces, not internal mass)
- Under-riser HVAC supply ducts (concrete/steel structure, not modeled as internal mass)
- Seat-number placards (plastic, negligible); cupholder graphics (negligible)
- Exit and emergency signage (LED, negligible)

### Reference Configuration

**300 m² multiplex cinema seating section (stadium configuration):**
- 350 fixed upholstered cinema seats
- Row pitch: 1.05 m (front-to-front; accounts for riser step depth)
- Seat width: 0.55 m (center-to-center); seat body: 0.50 m
- ~30 rows; ~12 seats per row average (variable — wider center rows, narrower side sections)
- 2 longitudinal center aisles; aisle width: 1.10 m
- Typical seating density: 0.857 m²/seat including aisle share
- Row end aisle standards: 2 per row × 30 rows = 60 standards
- Aisle step handrails: 2 aisles × 2 rails = 4 rails; effective length 9 m per rail

---

## Component Inventory

### 1. Fixed Cinema Seats (350 per 300 m²)

**Commercial Multiplex Stadium Seat (spring-loaded folding, fully upholstered, with integrated cup holder):**
- Seat body width: 0.50 m (within armrests); center-to-center spacing: 0.55 m
- Row pitch: 1.05 m (front-to-front)
- Seat pan depth (deployed): 0.46 m
- Seat back height above pan: 0.60 m (includes headrest zone)
- Seat pan pivot height: 0.46 m from floor (elevated for stadium riser geometry)
- Pedestal height: 0.43 m (floor to underside of structural frame)
- Pedestal diameter: 0.06 m (round hollow steel tube), 2 per seat
- Armrest: 0.40 m long × 0.05 m wide × 0.10 m high (hardwood cap over foam core)
- Cup holder: 1 per seat; OD 0.085 m, height 0.075 m, ABS plastic insert molded into armrest
- Back shell: ABS plastic decorative panel on rear face of seat back (visible to patron in next row)
- Construction: Hollow steel tube pedestals and structural frame; high-density polyurethane foam (seat and back); commercial fabric upholstery; solid hardwood armrest caps; ABS plastic cup holder insert and back shell; spring-loaded folding hinge and hardware

**Surface Area per Seat:**

*Seat Pan (folding — both faces exposed to room air):*
- Top (upholstered, fabric): 0.50 × 0.46 = 0.230 m²
- Bottom (exposed when seat folded): 0.50 × 0.46 = 0.230 m²
- Pivot edge cap: 0.50 × 0.02 = 0.010 m²
- **Seat Pan SA: 0.470 m²**

*Seat Back (both faces exposed to room air):*
- Front face (upholstered fabric): 0.50 × 0.60 = 0.300 m²
- Rear face (ABS plastic back shell): 0.50 × 0.60 = 0.300 m²
- Top cap: 0.50 × 0.02 = 0.010 m²
- **Seat Back SA: 0.610 m²**

*Armrests (1 effective per seat — adjacent seats share; row-end outer armrests counted with standards below):*
- Top: 0.05 × 0.40 = 0.020 m²
- Bottom: 0.05 × 0.40 = 0.020 m²
- Inner + outer sides: 2 × 0.10 × 0.40 = 0.080 m²
- Front + rear ends: 2 × 0.05 × 0.10 = 0.010 m²
- **Armrest SA: 0.130 m²**

*Cup Holder (1 per seat, OD 0.085 m, height 0.075 m, ABS plastic cylindrical insert):*
- Outer lateral surface: π × 0.085 × 0.075 = 0.020 m²
- Top annular ring (wall area): π/4 × (0.085² − 0.065²) = π/4 × 0.0030 = 0.002 m²
- **Cup Holder SA: 0.022 m²**

*Steel Pedestals (2 per seat, round hollow tube):*
- Lateral surface per pedestal: π × 0.06 × 0.43 = 0.0810 m²
- Top and base caps (2 × 2): 4 × π × 0.030² = 0.0113 m²
- Both pedestals: 2 × 0.0810 + 0.0113 = **0.173 m²**

*Under-Seat Structural Connecting Bar (1 per seat, rectangular hollow section):*
- 0.50 m long × 0.06 m tall × 0.03 m depth
- 2 × (0.50 × 0.06 + 0.50 × 0.03 + 0.06 × 0.03) = 2 × (0.030 + 0.015 + 0.002) = **0.094 m²**

**Total SA per Seat: 0.470 + 0.610 + 0.130 + 0.022 + 0.173 + 0.094 = 1.499 m²**

**Mass per Seat:**
- Steel frame (tube pedestals + connecting bars + folding hinge bracket): 5.0 kg
- Polyurethane foam (seat pan 50 mm + back 45 mm, approximate):
  - Seat pan: 0.50 × 0.46 × 0.050 × 35 = 0.403 kg
  - Back: 0.50 × 0.60 × 0.045 × 35 = 0.473 kg
  - Armrest foam core: 0.15 kg
  - Rounding with density variation: 1.0 kg foam base; use **1.7 kg** (accounts for 40–50 kg/m³ high-density commercial foam used in cinema seats for durability under high-cycle public use)
- Commercial fabric upholstery (seat, back, armrests): 0.8 kg
- ABS plastic (cup holder insert + decorative back shell panel): 0.6 kg
- Solid hardwood armrest caps: 1.0 kg
- Spring mechanism, pivot hardware, seat-number placard: 0.9 kg
- **Total Mass per Seat: 5.0 + 1.7 + 0.8 + 0.6 + 1.0 + 0.9 = 10.0 kg**

**Per Floor Area (350 seats in 300 m²):**
- Surface Area: (350 × 1.499) / 300 = 524.65 / 300 = **1.749 m²/m²**
- Mass: (350 × 10.0) / 300 = 3,500 / 300 = **11.667 kg/m²**

### 2. Row End Aisle Standards (60 per 300 m²)

**Structural Row End Caps (hollow square steel tube):**
- Section: 0.06 m × 0.06 m outer, 3 mm wall thickness
- Height: 0.90 m (floor to top of cap; matches taller cinema seat back)
- Finish: powder-coated steel; may include illuminated row letter plaque (negligible)

**Surface Area per Standard:**
- Four faces: 4 × 0.06 × 0.90 = 0.216 m²
- Top cap: 0.06 × 0.06 = 0.004 m²
- **Total SA per Standard: 0.220 m²** (use 0.222 m² including base plate edges)

- Mass: 6.84 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.90 × 7,800 = **4.80 kg**

**Per Floor Area (60 standards in 300 m²):**

### 3. Aisle Step Handrails (4 rails per 300 m²)

**Stadium Riser Step Handrails (round hollow steel tube):**
- Configuration: 2 center aisles × 2 rails per aisle = 4 rails
- Effective length per rail: 9 m (accounts for full stepped aisle run length including step transitions)
- Outer diameter: 0.038 m (1½-inch nominal pipe); wall thickness: 3 mm
- Finish: brushed stainless or powder-coated steel

**Surface Area per Rail:**

- End caps (2): 2 × π × 0.019² = 0.002 m²
- **Total SA per Rail: 1.076 m²**

**Per Floor Area (4 rails in 300 m²):**
- Surface Area: (4 × 1.076) / 300 = 4.304 / 300 = **0.014 m²/m²**
- Mass: (4 × 24.6) / 300 = 98.4 / 300 = **0.328 kg/m²**

## Component Summary Table

| Component | Qty / 300 m² | SA / Unit (m²) | Mass / Unit (kg) | SA / m² Floor | Mass / m² Floor | Primary Material |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|------------------|---------------|-----------------|-----------------|

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Material Breakdown by Mass:**

*Steel (seat frames, folding mechanisms, spring hardware, row standards, handrails):*
- Seat frame (pedestals, bars, hinge brackets): 5.0 × 350 / 300 = 5.833 kg/m²
- Spring mechanism and hardware: 0.9 × 350 / 300 = 1.050 kg/m²
- Row end standards: 0.960 kg/m²
- Aisle step handrails: 0.328 kg/m²
- **Total steel: 8.171 kg/m²** (63.1%)

*Polyurethane foam (seat and back cushioning):*
- 1.7 × 350 / 300 = **1.983 kg/m²** (15.3%)

*Commercial fabric upholstery (seat, back, armrests):*
- 0.8 × 350 / 300 = **0.933 kg/m²** (7.2%)

*ABS plastic (cup holders + decorative back shell panels):*
- 0.6 × 350 / 300 = **0.700 kg/m²** (5.4%)

*Solid hardwood (armrest caps):*
- 1.0 × 350 / 300 = **1.167 kg/m²** (9.0%)

**Total: 8.171 + 1.983 + 0.933 + 0.700 + 1.167 = 12.954 kg/m²** ✓

### Volume Fractions (for Conductivity Weighting)

```
V_i = mass_i / density_i  [m³ per m² of floor area]

Steel:    8.171 / 7,800  = 0.001047 m³/m²
Foam:     1.983 /    35  = 0.056657 m³/m²
Fabric:   0.933 /   550  = 0.001696 m³/m²
Plastic:  0.700 / 1,050  = 0.000667 m³/m²
Hardwood: 1.167 /   700  = 0.001667 m³/m²

V_total = 0.001047 + 0.056657 + 0.001696 + 0.000667 + 0.001667 = 0.061734 m³/m²

Volume fractions:
  Steel:    0.001047 / 0.061734 = 1.696%
  Foam:     0.056657 / 0.061734 = 91.77%
  Fabric:   0.001696 / 0.061734 = 2.747%
  Plastic:  0.000667 / 0.061734 = 1.080%
  Hardwood: 0.001667 / 0.061734 = 2.700%
```

> Polyurethane foam occupies 91.8% of composite volume despite contributing only 15.3% of composite mass. This is the defining characteristic of cinema seating thermal mass, shared with performing arts auditorium seating: the foam cushioning (~35–50 kg/m³ high-density commercial grade) is the volumetrically dominant material. Steel, though 63.1% of the mass, occupies only 1.7% of the volume. The ABS plastic components (cup holders and back shells) contribute meaningfully to both volume (1.1%) and mass (5.4%) — distinguishing this space type from the performing arts auditorium.

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Total mass / Total volume
            = 12.954 / 0.061734
            = 209.8 kg/m³  →  210 kg/m³
```

> The very low composite density (210 kg/m³) reflects foam-volume dominance, consistent with the performing arts auditorium (219 kg/m³). The slight reduction relative to the auditorium is attributable to the cinema seat's somewhat higher foam volume (wider and deeper seat pan and taller back) combined with a slightly smaller seat count per floor area (1.17 seats/m² vs. 1.50 seats/m²).

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Material properties:
  Steel:    460 J/kg·K   (carbon steel)
  Foam:   1,700 J/kg·K   (polyurethane foam, open/semi-open cell)
  Fabric: 1,340 J/kg·K   (commercial textile)
  Plastic: 1,400 J/kg·K  (ABS thermoplastic)
  Hardwood: 1,700 J/kg·K (solid hardwood)

Steel:    8.171 × 460   = 3,759
Foam:     1.983 × 1,700 = 3,371
Fabric:   0.933 × 1,340 = 1,250
Plastic:  0.700 × 1,400 =   980
Hardwood: 1.167 × 1,700 = 1,984

c_p,composite = (3,759 + 3,371 + 1,250 + 980 + 1,984) / 12.954
              = 11,344 / 12.954
              = 875.7 J/kg·K  →  876 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity (Volume-Weighted)

```
k_composite = Σ(V_frac_i × k_i)

Material conductivities:
  Steel:    50.0 W/m·K   (carbon steel)
  Foam:     0.038 W/m·K  (polyurethane foam, typical)
  Fabric:   0.06 W/m·K   (textile)
  Plastic:  0.17 W/m·K   (ABS thermoplastic)
  Hardwood: 0.15 W/m·K   (hardwood, across grain)

Steel:    0.01696 × 50.0  = 0.848
Foam:     0.91770 × 0.038 = 0.035
Fabric:   0.02747 × 0.06  = 0.002
Plastic:  0.01080 × 0.17  = 0.002
Hardwood: 0.02700 × 0.15  = 0.004

k_composite ≈ 0.848 + 0.035 + 0.002 + 0.002 + 0.004
            ≈ 0.891 W/m·K
```

> Steel at 1.7% of total volume contributes 0.848 W/m·K — 95.2% of composite conductivity. Foam at 91.8% of volume contributes only 0.035 W/m·K. ABS plastic (1.1% volume, k = 0.17 W/m·K) and hardwood (2.7% volume, k = 0.15 W/m·K) each contribute 0.002–0.004 W/m·K. As with the performing arts auditorium, the steel pedestals and frame act as thermal bridges through the insulating foam body of each seat; the effective composite conductivity is dominated by the steel skeleton despite its tiny volume fraction.

### Effective Thickness

```
t_eff = Total mass per m² / (SA_ratio × composite density)
      = 12.954 / (1.81 × 210)
      = 12.954 / 380.1
      = 0.03408 m  ≈  0.034 m  (34 mm)
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 210 × 876
    = 183,960 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Foam-Volume-Dominated Space — Closely Related to Performing Arts Auditorium:**
- Very low composite density (210 kg/m³) — nearly identical to the performing arts auditorium (219 kg/m³); polyurethane foam at 35 kg/m³ occupies 91.8% of composite volume; the cinema seat's wider and deeper form factor marginally increases foam volume share relative to the auditorium seat
- Moderate SA ratio (1.81 m²/m²) — lower than the performing arts auditorium (2.11 m²/m²) primarily because of lower seating density (1.17 seats/m² vs. 1.50 seats/m²); each cinema seat generates slightly more SA per seat (1.499 m² vs. 1.347 m²) due to larger dimensions, but the density difference dominates
- Similar specific heat (876 J/kg·K) — the addition of ABS plastic (c_p = 1,400 J/kg·K, 5.4% of mass) in place of some fabric and hardwood content modestly raises the composite specific heat slightly above the auditorium (859 J/kg·K); foam and hardwood (1,700 J/kg·K each) continue to pull the composite well above steel's 460 J/kg·K
- Slightly lower conductivity (0.891 W/m·K vs. 0.966 W/m·K) — reflects the marginally lower steel volume fraction (1.7% vs. 1.85%) as the foam body of cinema seats is proportionally larger; the reduction is physically meaningful but small in absolute terms

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Low thermal capacitance per unit volume (183,960 J/m³·K) — closely matching the performing arts auditorium (188,121 J/m³·K); both seating zones respond relatively quickly to zone air temperature changes because foam is the volumetrically dominant material with low mass-per-volume heat storage
- Moderate total thermal mass (12.96 kg/m²) — somewhat lower than the performing arts auditorium (15.36 kg/m²) due to lower seating density; the per-seat mass (10.0 kg) is higher than the auditorium (9.0 kg), but with only 1.17 seats/m² versus 1.50 seats/m², the floor-area-normalized mass is lower
- The ABS plastic back shell panels, while low conductivity, provide a continuous exposed surface at the rear of each seat row; these surfaces exchange heat directly with the zone air circulation during pre-conditioning cycles
- Cup holders (steel or plastic depending on insert type) present high surface-area-to-mass ratio elements at armrest height; in zones with top-discharge or ceiling-supply HVAC, these horizontal exposed surfaces participate actively in convective heat exchange

### Design Appropriateness

**Motion Picture Theater — Distinctive from Performing Arts Auditorium:**
- **Lower seating density is the primary differentiator** (1.17 seats/m² vs. 1.50 seats/m²) — modern cinema seats are noticeably wider (0.55 m c-to-c vs. 0.52 m), deeper (0.46 m seat pan vs. 0.43 m), and have wider armrests with cup holders; the resulting row pitch (1.05 m vs. 0.90 m) substantially reduces seats per floor area; this is the main driver of the lower SA ratio and total mass compared to performing arts venues
- **Cup holders are the defining new material element** (ABS plastic, 5.4% of total mass) — not present in performing arts auditorium seats; cinema patrons expect cup holder access for beverages throughout the screening, making this a standard fixture in all modern multiplex seating; the ABS back shell panel is similarly ubiquitous in commercial cinema seating, providing a durable surface that protects the foam core from the patron in the row behind
- **Similar foam-dominant thermal profile** to the performing arts auditorium — both are fundamentally "steel frame + polyurethane foam + fabric" systems; the addition of ABS plastic in the cinema seat does not materially change the foam-dominated thermal character of the space
- **Stadium riser handrails are shorter and fewer than performing arts aisle handrails** (4 rails × 9 m vs. 8 rails × 12 m) — cinema aisles are typically fewer and shorter (2 center aisles vs. 4 longitudinal aisles in an auditorium); total steel handrail mass contribution is correspondingly lower (0.328 kg/m² vs. 0.618 kg/m²), but the step geometry of the riser transitions exposes handrail steel surfaces to more direct airflow from HVAC risers between rows

### Comparison to Related Seating Space Types

| Parameter | Motion Picture Theater | Auditorium (Perf. Arts) | Convention Center |
|-----------|----------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| SA Ratio (m²/m²) | 1.81 | 2.11 | 1.05 |
| Mass (kg/m²) | 12.96 | 15.36 | 5.58 |
| Density (kg/m³) | 210 | 219 | 636 |
| Conductivity (W/m-K) | 0.891 | 0.966 | 3.73 |
| Specific Heat (J/kg·K) | 876 | 859 | 562 |
| Thermal Capacitance (J/m³·K) | 183,960 | 188,121 | 357,432 |
| Dominant volume material | PU foam | PU foam | Metal folding chairs |
| Seats/m² | 1.17 | 1.50 | ~1.80 (folding) |

> The motion picture theater and performing arts auditorium share a fundamentally foam-dominated thermal profile (very low density and capacitance per unit volume), but the cinema achieves this at a lower seating density — yielding a lower SA ratio and total mass per floor area. Both contrast sharply with the convention center seating area, where lightweight metal folding/stacking chairs produce a much higher composite density (636 kg/m³) despite the high seat count; the folding chair's thin-gauge steel construction results in high metal volume fraction, pulling density and conductivity far above the cushioned-seat spaces. The convention center's lower total mass (5.58 kg/m²) relative to both cushioned-seat venues underscores the thermal mass contribution of foam cushioning — which, despite its low density, adds meaningful mass when present in seat pan and back thicknesses of 40–50 mm per component.

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Cinema auditoriums operate on a high-frequency bimodal schedule: full occupancy during screenings (multiple showings per day) versus near-zero occupancy between screenings and during dark periods; pre-conditioning windows of 20–40 minutes between screenings must recover the zone from the post-occupancy heat load condition
- High occupant density during screenings (350 persons in 300 m² = 1.17 p/m²) produces substantial sensible and latent loads; the seated patrons' body heat and respiration dominate thermal exchange in the zone during screenings; internal mass effects are secondary during peak occupancy
- Zonal HVAC supply is typically ceiling-mounted in cinema auditoriums (unlike under-seat displacement ventilation more common in performing arts venues); ceiling supply increases air mixing in the zone, elevating convective coefficients at internal mass surfaces relative to low-velocity displacement systems
- The stepped riser geometry creates micro-climate variations along the seating rake — lower rows receive cooler supply air from ceiling diffusers first; internal mass thermal lag at lower rows may differ from upper rows; EnergyPlus models the zone as thermally uniform, which is an acceptable simplification for most energy modeling purposes

**Operational Patterns:**
- Multiplex cinemas typically operate 5–8 screenings per day per auditorium for major releases; smaller screens may have 3–4 screenings per day
- Pre-conditioning: 20–40 minutes before showtime; shorter recovery window than performing arts venues means pre-conditioning must begin from a lighter setback condition
- Screening duration: 90–180 minutes (typical feature film); shorter than many performing arts events but with more frequent occupancy cycling per day
- Between-show window: 15–30 minutes (cleanup + seating); zone transitions from post-occupancy warmth to incoming cool audience; the internal mass (foam body of seats) moderates temperature swings during this rapid transition
- Dark-day setback: when a screen goes dark (no bookings), full setback is achievable; the foam mass will equilibrate to setback temperature within 1–2 hours given its low thermal capacitance

**Special Considerations:**
- **Premium large-format (PLF) and IMAX screens** are typically larger auditoriums (400–800 seats) with higher ceiling heights; the per-seat internal mass definition (`AudienceSeating_MotionPictureTheater_IntMass`) applies to these larger screens with appropriate adjustment if seat density differs materially from the reference configuration
- **Recliner-configuration cinema auditoriums** are increasingly common in premium cinema contexts; recliners are substantially larger (0.75–0.90 m wide, 1.20–1.50 m row pitch when deployed), have higher foam volume, and typically have individual motorized footrests; the reference definition underestimates internal mass for recliner cinemas — a dedicated recliner seat definition would add approximately 40–60% to the per-seat foam volume and increase armrest mass due to dual cup holders and larger hardwood/plastic armrest structures; seating density in recliner cinemas may fall to 0.50–0.80 seats/m², further reducing the SA ratio per floor area
- **Drive-in theaters** are a distinct building type (outdoor, no fixed internal mass) and are not applicable to this definition
- **Screen acoustic panels** (perforated fabric or microperforated acoustic panels at the screen wall) are structural elements and should be modeled as opaque wall surfaces, not as internal mass objects; their thermal mass is captured in the zone envelope model

---

*End of Calculation Report*

# Internal Mass Calculations: CS Audience Seating Area - Penitentiary

**Report Date:** April 9, 2026
**Scope:** Audience Seating Area – Penitentiary Space Type
**Purpose:** Calculate OpenStudio InternalMass properties for thermal modeling

---

## CS Audience Seating Area - Penitentiary

### Space Characteristics

**Typical Occupancy:** 100–250 inmates (program-driven; scheduled sessions with officers present)
**Floor Area:** 150–300 m² (seating area proper, excluding officer station, entry vestibule, and AV/projection alcove); reference area: **200 m²**
**Ceiling Height:** 3.0–4.0 m (flat or minimal slope; lower than civilian auditoriums due to security sight-line requirements and structural constraints typical of correctional construction)
**Function:** Fixed-seat audience seating for institutional programming — religious services, educational presentations, in-house film screenings, counseling sessions, and similar group programming in medium- to maximum-security correctional facilities. The space is bounded by the seating deck: rows of fixed bolted-down steel tablet-arm chairs, cross aisles, and perimeter aisle security handrails. The officer station, entry vestibule, security vestibule, and AV control alcove are modeled as separate zones. The reference configuration models a single-level programming room of a medium-security state correctional facility.

**Key Features:**
- Fixed institutional steel tablet-arm chairs bolted to concrete floor (the dominant element)
- All-metal construction — no upholstery, foam, or wood permitted (security policy eliminates concealment hazards)
- Tamper-resistant, ligature-resistant hardware throughout (security hex fasteners, no exposed anchors)
- Perforated steel seat pans and backs (anti-pooling, anti-concealment, tamper-resistance)
- Powder-coated finish in institutional gray or tan
- Aisle security handrails (steel pipe, defines officer circulation paths)
- Floor-mounted row dividers (steel angle, separates seating zones — not modeled separately; negligible SA)
- AV projection screen housing (steel, wall-mounted; modeled within perimeter construction zone)
- No decorative elements, no acoustic treatment panels, no planters, no seat-number placards

### Reference Configuration

**200 m² penitentiary programming room seating section:**
- 200 fixed steel tablet-arm chairs
- Row pitch: 0.90 m (front-to-front); security spacing allows slightly wider clearance than civilian venues but rows are still closely packed under most facility standards
- Seat width: 0.55 m (center-to-center); tablet arm extends to the right, shared aisle to the left
- ~22 rows; ~9 seats per row average
- 2 longitudinal aisles; aisle width: 1.20 m (officer patrol clearance requirement)
- Typical seating density: 1.00 seat/m² (including aisle share)
- Aisle handrails: 2 aisles × 2 rails per aisle = 4 rails; effective length per rail: 10 m

---

## Component Inventory

### 1. Fixed Steel Tablet-Arm Chairs (200 per 200 m²)

**Institutional Security-Grade Tablet-Arm Chair (all-steel, floor-bolted):**
- Seat pan width: 0.41 m; seat pan depth: 0.38 m
- Seat pan material: 14-gauge (1.9 mm) perforated steel plate; perforation pattern reduces plate mass by approximately 25% while maintaining projected surface area
- Seat back width: 0.40 m; seat back height: 0.46 m
- Seat back material: 14-gauge (1.9 mm) solid steel plate
- Tablet arm: 0.30 m × 0.25 m × 3/16-inch (4.76 mm) solid steel plate
- Main frame: 1-inch square tube (25 mm OD, 16-gauge / 1.6 mm wall, welded), total frame length: 2.8 m (four legs + two side rails + two cross braces)
- Tablet arm support: 1-inch round tube (25 mm OD, 16-gauge), length: 0.30 m
- Floor anchors: 4 × 1/2-inch carriage bolts with security nuts, cast into concrete (mass and SA negligible)
- Finish: institutional powder coat; tamper-resistant fasteners throughout

**Surface Area per Chair:**

*Seat Pan (perforated steel plate — top and bottom faces equally exposed to room air):*
- Top face: 0.41 × 0.38 = 0.156 m²
- Bottom face: 0.41 × 0.38 = 0.156 m²
- Front edge cap: 0.41 × 0.0019 = 0.001 m²
- Side edge caps: 2 × 0.38 × 0.0019 = 0.001 m²
- **Seat Pan SA: 0.314 m²**

*Seat Back (solid steel plate — front and rear faces both exposed):*
- Front face: 0.40 × 0.46 = 0.184 m²
- Rear face: 0.40 × 0.46 = 0.184 m²
- Top edge: 0.40 × 0.0019 = 0.001 m²
- Side edges: 2 × 0.46 × 0.0019 = 0.002 m²
- **Seat Back SA: 0.371 m²**

*Tablet Arm (solid steel plate — top and bottom faces exposed):*
- Top face: 0.30 × 0.25 = 0.075 m²
- Bottom face: 0.30 × 0.25 = 0.075 m²
- Perimeter edges: 2 × (0.30 + 0.25) × 0.00476 = 0.005 m²
- **Tablet Arm SA: 0.155 m²**

*Main Frame (square tube, 2.8 m total length):*
- Lateral surface: 4 sides × 0.025 m × 2.8 m = 0.280 m²
- End caps (negligible for welded assembly)
- **Frame SA: 0.280 m²**

*Tablet Arm Support (round tube, 0.30 m):*
- Lateral surface: π × 0.025 × 0.30 = 0.024 m²
- **Support SA: 0.024 m²**

**Total SA per Chair: 0.314 + 0.371 + 0.155 + 0.280 + 0.024 = 1.144 m²**

**Mass per Chair:**
- Seat pan (14-gauge perforated, 25% mass reduction for perforations): 0.41 × 0.38 × 0.0019 × 7,800 × 0.75 = **1.73 kg**
- Seat back (14-gauge solid plate): 0.40 × 0.46 × 0.0019 × 7,800 = **2.73 kg**
- Tablet arm (3/16-inch solid plate): 0.30 × 0.25 × 0.00476 × 7,800 = **2.79 kg**
- Main frame (square tube, cross-section area = 0.025² − 0.0218² = 1.50 × 10⁻⁴ m²): 1.50 × 10⁻⁴ × 2.8 × 7,800 = **3.28 kg**
- Tablet arm support (round tube, cross-section area = π/4 × (0.025² − 0.0218²) = 1.178 × 10⁻⁴ m²): 1.178 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.30 × 7,800 = **0.28 kg**
- Anchor hardware (4 bolts, nuts, washers): **0.50 kg**
- **Total Mass per Chair: 1.73 + 2.73 + 2.79 + 3.28 + 0.28 + 0.50 = 11.31 kg**

**Per Floor Area (200 chairs in 200 m²):**
- Surface Area: (200 × 1.144) / 200 = 228.8 / 200 = **1.144 m²/m²**
- Mass: (200 × 11.31) / 200 = 2,262 / 200 = **11.31 kg/m²**

### 2. Aisle Security Handrails (4 rails per 200 m²)

**Institutional Aisle Handrails (round hollow steel tube, wall-mounted brackets):**
- Configuration: 2 longitudinal aisles × 2 rails per aisle = 4 rails
- Effective length per rail: 10 m
- Outer diameter: 0.048 m (1½-inch nominal pipe, schedule 40); wall thickness: 3.7 mm
- Finish: powder-coated steel or galvanized; bracket hardware negligible

**Surface Area per Rail:**
- Lateral surface: π × 0.048 × 10 = 1.508 m²
- End caps (2): 2 × π × 0.024² = 0.004 m²
- **Total SA per Rail: 1.512 m²**

**Mass per Rail:**
- Schedule 40, 1½-inch pipe unit weight: 2.73 kg/m
- Mass: 2.73 × 10 = **27.3 kg** per rail

**Per Floor Area (4 rails in 200 m²):**
- Surface Area: (4 × 1.512) / 200 = 6.048 / 200 = **0.030 m²/m²**
- Mass: (4 × 27.3) / 200 = 109.2 / 200 = **0.546 kg/m²**

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Material Breakdown by Mass:**

*Steel (all chair components — seat pans, seat backs, tablet arms, frames, supports, anchors; all aisle handrails):*
- Chairs: 11.31 kg/m² (all steel components)
- Aisle handrails: 0.546 kg/m²
- **Total steel: 11.856 kg/m²** (100.0%)

> This space type is unique among audience seating categories in being composed entirely of a single material — steel. Security policy in correctional facilities prohibits upholstered, foam-cushioned, or wood-component furniture because such materials provide concealment opportunities for contraband and are not ligature-resistant. The result is a thermally simple, single-material composite with no volume-fraction weighting ambiguity.

### Volume Fractions (for Conductivity Weighting)

```
V_i = mass_i / density_i  [m³ per m² of floor area]

Steel (all):  11.856 / 7,800  = 0.001520 m³/m²

V_total = 0.001520 m³/m²

Volume fraction:
  Steel:  0.001520 / 0.001520 = 100.0%
```

> The composite volume per unit floor area (0.001520 m³/m²) is very small — reflecting the thin-wall hollow tube and plate construction of institutional steel furniture. Although steel accounts for 100% of both mass and volume, the actual volume occupied by solid steel within each chair's overall geometric envelope is a small fraction of that envelope; the remainder is open air within the seat structure, which EnergyPlus handles implicitly through the internal mass surface area and convection boundary conditions.

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Total mass / Total volume
            = 11.856 / 0.001520
            = 7,800 kg/m³
```

> Single-material composite; density equals that of carbon steel. No volume-fraction blending required. This is the highest composite density of any audience seating space type — the absence of low-density foam, fabric, or wood (all of which dilute density in civilian seating) results in a composite at full steel density.

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Material properties:
  Steel:  460 J/kg·K  (carbon steel, all components)

c_p,composite = (11.856 × 460) / 11.856
              = 460 J/kg·K
```

> Single-material composite; specific heat equals that of carbon steel. This is the lowest specific heat of any audience seating space type — steel's 460 J/kg·K is well below the 1,340–1,700 J/kg·K range of the organic materials (foam, fabric, hardwood) present in upholstered civilian seating.

### Weighted Average Conductivity (Volume-Weighted)

```
k_composite = Σ(V_frac_i × k_i)

Material conductivities:
  Steel:  50.0 W/m·K  (carbon steel)

k_composite = 1.000 × 50.0
            = 50.0 W/m·K
```

> Single-material composite; conductivity equals that of carbon steel. This is the highest conductivity of any audience seating space type by a substantial margin — the steel frame chairs and handrails exchange heat with room air rapidly, with no insulating foam body to impede heat flow as in upholstered civilian seats (where foam at 91.5% volume fraction reduces effective conductivity to ~0.97 W/m·K despite steel structural components). The practical implication is that the penitentiary seating thermal mass responds very quickly to changes in zone air temperature.

### Effective Thickness

```
t_eff = Total mass per m² / (SA_ratio × composite density)
      = 11.856 / (1.174 × 7,800)
      = 11.856 / 9,157.2
      = 0.001294 m  ≈  0.0013 m  (1.3 mm)
```

> The very thin equivalent slab thickness (1.3 mm) is characteristic of thin-wall hollow metal furniture — the composite mass per unit floor area (11.86 kg/m²) is spread across a relatively large surface area (1.174 m²/m²) at high steel density (7,800 kg/m³). This thickness is consistent with the 14-gauge (1.9 mm) plate and 16-gauge (1.6 mm) tube construction: the equivalent slab is thinner than the individual plate gauges because the total surface area exposed to room air exceeds the total projected cross-sectional area of the furniture.

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 7,800 × 460
    = 3,588,000 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Steel-Dominant Space — Highest Composite Density of Any Seating Category:**
- Very high composite density (7,800 kg/m³) — the maximum possible for carbon steel; no low-density dilutants (foam, fabric, wood) are present; this is the defining physical consequence of security-driven all-metal furniture policy
- Moderate SA ratio (1.17 m²/m²) — lower than civilian auditorium seating (2.11 m²/m²) for two reasons: (1) the tablet-arm chair generates less surface area per seat than a fully upholstered theater seat (1.144 vs 1.347 m²/seat) because it lacks a folding seat pan mechanism and row-end outer side panels; (2) seating density is lower (1.00 vs 1.50 seats/m²) due to officer patrol clearance requirements in correctional facilities
- Very low specific heat (460 J/kg·K) — the lowest of any audience seating space type; steel's 460 J/kg·K is substantially below the organic materials that dominate civilian seating composites (foam 1,700; fabric 1,340; hardwood 1,700)
- Very high conductivity (50.0 W/m·K) — the highest of any seating-category space type by far; all-steel construction presents no insulating barriers to heat conduction through the furniture body; contrast with the performing arts auditorium (0.966 W/m·K) where foam at 91.5% volume fraction suppresses effective conductivity to near-foam values despite a steel structural frame

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Very high thermal capacitance per unit volume (3,588,000 J/m³·K) — the highest of any audience seating space type, reflecting steel's combination of high density and moderate specific heat; however, the total volume of steel per unit floor area is very small (0.001520 m³/m²), so the actual thermal energy stored per m² of floor area is moderate
- Moderate total thermal mass per floor area (11.86 kg/m²) — comparable to other seating-category space types despite radically different material composition; the all-steel chairs are heavier per unit than upholstered theater seats but are present at lower density
- Very rapid thermal response — steel's high conductivity and lack of insulating foam volume means the chair surfaces equilibrate with room air temperature almost instantaneously relative to HVAC time scales; the effective thermal time constant of a steel tube chair is seconds to low minutes, versus the tens of minutes characteristic of foam-upholstered theater seats
- Convective exchange at steel surfaces is direct and efficient — no insulating fabric or foam layer impedes heat transfer from metal surface to room air; the convection boundary condition at metal surfaces is active at the full room-air convective coefficient

### Design Appropriateness

**Penitentiary Audience Seating — Distinctive Thermal Profile:**
- **Security policy drives material selection completely** — the all-steel construction is not a cost measure; institutional-grade tablet-arm chairs are more expensive per unit than basic civilian folding chairs; the all-metal requirement reflects ligature-resistance, concealment-prevention, and durability standards that are mandatory under correctional facility design guidelines; the thermal modeling must reflect this physical reality
- **Tablet-arm chairs are the overwhelmingly dominant component** (95.4% of mass, 97.4% of SA) — even more dominant than the theater seat in a performing arts auditorium (87.9% of mass), because the only other element present (aisle handrails) is a minor steel element; there are no planters, no display cases, no decorative elements, and no acoustic panels that would add secondary mass contributions
- **Perforated seat pans are a security design element with thermal implications** — perforation reduces seat pan mass by approximately 25% relative to solid plate, while maintaining approximately the same projected surface area; the effect is captured by the 0.75 mass reduction factor applied in the calculation; the perforations also improve air circulation under the seat, potentially increasing the effective convective exchange coefficient at the seat pan lower surface
- **Aisle handrails are minor contributors** (4.6% of mass, 2.6% of SA) — consistent with other seating space types where handrails contribute a modest fraction of total thermal mass; in penitentiary configurations, handrails serve a dual function as security control elements (limiting inmate movement across aisles) and safety fall-protection rails

### Comparison to Related Seating Space Types

| Parameter | Penitentiary Seating | Auditorium Seating | Convention Center Seating |
|-----------|---------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| SA Ratio (m²/m²) | 1.17 | 2.11 | 0.70 |
| Mass (kg/m²) | 11.86 | 15.36 | 5.94 |
| Density (kg/m³) | 7,800 | 219 | 7,800 |
| Conductivity (W/m-K) | 50.0 | 0.966 | 50.0 |
| Specific Heat (J/kg·K) | 460 | 859 | 460 |
| Thermal Capacitance (J/m³·K) | 3,588,000 | 188,121 | 3,588,000 |
| Dominant volume material | Steel | PU foam | Steel |
| Seats/m² | 1.00 | 1.50 | 0.35 (portable) |

> The penitentiary and convention center seating share identical material properties (both all-steel constructions), but differ substantially in SA ratio and mass per floor area — the penitentiary has fixed bolted-down chairs at 1.00 seat/m² versus portable folding chairs at 0.35 seat/m² in the convention center. The auditorium seating's foam-dominated composite is thermally inverted: its density (219 kg/m³) is 36× lower, its conductivity is 52× lower, and its thermal capacitance is 19× lower than the penitentiary's all-steel composite — yet its total mass per floor area (15.36 kg/m²) exceeds the penitentiary's because of the higher seat count (1.5 vs 1.0 seats/m²) and heavier per-seat mass driven by the hardwood armrest caps and foam cushioning.

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Penitentiary programming rooms operate on a rigid institutional schedule: occupancy during scheduled program sessions (typically 1–3 hours) with full setback between sessions; the HVAC system is not subject to the event-driven surge demands of performing arts venues but must handle the 100–250-person latent load during sessions
- All-steel seating responds rapidly to temperature changes — pre-conditioning the seating zone before a session requires substantially less lead time than upholstered civilian seating, because the steel chairs equilibrate with zone air within minutes; however, the steel chairs also release stored heat rapidly after a session, which may create overshoot conditions if setback is imposed immediately after a high-occupancy session
- Sensible and latent loads from 200 inmates in 200 m² (full occupancy) are high — approximately 200 × 90 W sensible + 200 × 60 W latent = 18 kW sensible + 12 kW latent in 200 m²; these loads dominate over internal mass thermal storage contributions during sessions
- Absence of under-seat ventilation supply (common in civilian auditoriums but not standard in correctional facilities) means air distribution is typically overhead, reducing the direct exchange between supply air and seat surfaces that would otherwise enhance convective heat exchange coefficients

**Operational Patterns:**
- Program schedule: rigid — typically 2–4 sessions per day for active programming rooms; sessions are scheduled by facility management, not demand-driven
- Pre-session conditioning: 30–45 minutes sufficient (faster recovery than civilian auditoriums due to rapid steel thermal response)
- Session duration: 1–3 hours typical; occupancy is essentially binary (full or empty) with no intermission movement
- Between sessions: full setback possible; steel chairs cool or warm to ambient quickly, so the thermal zone is responsive to setback/recovery commands
- Overnight: complete setback; the low thermal time constant of steel furniture means the zone air temperature closely tracks the setpoint throughout the setback period with minimal thermal mass buffering

**Special Considerations:**
- **Security clearances between sessions** — inmates must exit and officers conduct clearance sweeps before the next group enters; this creates definite inter-session vacancy periods that are ideal for HVAC setback; the EnergyPlus schedule for this space type should reflect these definite occupancy blocks rather than the fractional or graduated occupancy profiles common in civilian venues
- **No acoustic treatment** — the absence of acoustic wall panels means the room has high ambient reverberation time; HVAC air distribution systems must be low-noise regardless, but there is no acoustic fabric absorber material contributing to internal mass as in some civilian assembly spaces; the wall and ceiling construction thermal mass is modeled through the envelope objects, not internal mass
- **Facility security level effects** — higher-security facilities (maximum vs medium) may have heavier-gauge chair construction (12-gauge vs 14-gauge plate), which would increase per-chair mass by approximately 25–30%; this calculation uses 14-gauge as representative of medium-security design; maximum-security facilities should apply a mass multiplier of approximately 1.25 to the per-chair values before recalculating SA ratio and thickness
- **Potential for folding chair deployment** — some lower-security correctional programming rooms use folding steel chairs rather than permanently bolted tablet-arm chairs; the per-chair SA and mass are similar for folding institutional chairs, but the seating density and layout may differ; the material properties (all-steel) and equivalent material definition remain valid for either configuration

---

*End of Calculation Report*

# Internal Mass Calculations: CS Audience Seating Area - Performing Arts Theater

**Report Date:** April 9, 2026
**Scope:** Audience Seating Area – Performing Arts Theater Space Type
**Purpose:** Calculate OpenStudio InternalMass properties for thermal modeling

---

## CS Audience Seating Area - Performing Arts Theater

### Space Characteristics

**Typical Occupancy:** 150–1,200 patrons (event-driven; near-zero between events)
**Floor Area:** 150–1,500 m² (seating deck only, excluding stage, orchestra pit, and backstage); reference area: **350 m²**
**Ceiling Height:** 7–15 m (sloped ceiling over raked seating deck; fly tower and balcony structure above)
**Function:** Fixed-seat audience seating for live theatrical performances — plays, musicals, opera, dance, and chamber concerts. The space is bounded by the seating deck proper: rows of fixed upholstered seats, cross aisles, side aisles, perimeter paths, and the side wall surfaces at the seat level. Distinctive features relative to a general auditorium include: a proscenium arch framing the stage opening, an orchestra pit at the front edge of the seating deck (separated by a safety barrier rail), a permanently installed sound mixing console at the rear of the house, and higher-end interior finishes reflecting the performing arts center aesthetic. The stage, proscenium, orchestra pit, fly tower, and backstage are modeled as separate zones. Balcony seating levels may be modeled as separate zones or aggregated. The reference configuration models a single-level main-floor seating section of a mid-size regional performing arts theater.

**Key Features:**
- Fixed upholstered theater seats in raked rows (dominant element)
- Folding seat mechanism (spring-loaded, steel)
- Upholstered armrests (shared between adjacent seats)
- Row end aisle standards (hollow square steel tube, powder-coated)
- Sloped aisle handrails (steel pipe)
- Orchestra pit safety barrier rail at front edge of seating deck (steel pipe)
- Sound mixing console and equipment rack (rear of house, fixed position)
- Under-seat HVAC supply plenums (structural floor — not modeled as internal mass)
- Seat-number placards, row letters, and decorative sconce bases (negligible)
- Exit signage and house lighting fixtures at seat level (negligible)

### Reference Configuration

**350 m² performing arts theater seating section:**
- 490 fixed upholstered theater seats
- Row pitch: 0.95 m (front-to-front; slightly more generous than large-format auditorium)
- Seat width: 0.52 m (center-to-center); seat body: 0.44 m
- ~47 rows; ~10–11 seats per row average (variable — wider center rows, narrower side sections)
- 2 longitudinal side aisles + 2 cross aisles; aisle width: 1.10 m
- Typical seating density: 0.714 m²/seat (including aisle share)
- Row end aisle standards: 2 per row × 47 rows = 94 standards
- Aisle handrails: 4 aisles × 2 rails × 11 m effective length = 8 rails
- Orchestra pit barrier rail: 1 rail × 12 m (front of seating deck)
- Sound mixing console: 1 unit (rear of house, fixed position)

## Component Inventory

### 1. Fixed Upholstered Theater Seats (490 per 350 m²)

**Commercial Performing Arts Seat (spring-loaded folding, fully upholstered):**
- Seat body width: 0.44 m (within armrests); center-to-center spacing: 0.52 m
- Row pitch: 0.95 m (front-to-front)
- Seat pan depth (deployed): 0.44 m
- Seat back height above pan: 0.58 m
- Seat pan pivot height: 0.46 m from floor
- Pedestal height: 0.40 m (floor to underside of structural frame)
- Pedestal diameter: 0.06 m (round hollow steel tube), 2 per seat
- Armrest: 0.35 m long × 0.04 m wide × 0.08 m high (hardwood)
- Construction: Hollow steel tube pedestals and structural frame; high-density polyurethane foam (seat and back, thicker gauge than large-format auditorium seats for comfort and durability); velvet or premium commercial fabric upholstery; solid hardwood armrest caps; spring-loaded folding hinge and hardware

**Surface Area per Seat:**

*Seat Pan (folding — both faces exposed to room air):*
- Top (upholstered, fabric): 0.44 × 0.44 = 0.194 m²
- Bottom (exposed when seat folded): 0.44 × 0.44 = 0.194 m²
- Pivot edge cap: 0.44 × 0.02 = 0.009 m²
- **Seat Pan SA: 0.397 m²**

*Seat Back (both faces exposed to room air):*
- Front face (upholstered): 0.44 × 0.58 = 0.255 m²
- Rear face (fabric/vinyl): 0.44 × 0.58 = 0.255 m²
- Top cap: 0.44 × 0.02 = 0.009 m²
- **Seat Back SA: 0.519 m²**

*Armrests (1 effective per seat — adjacent seats share; row-end outer armrests counted below):*
- Top: 0.04 × 0.35 = 0.014 m²
- Bottom: 0.04 × 0.35 = 0.014 m²
- Inner + outer sides: 2 × 0.08 × 0.35 = 0.056 m²
- Front + rear ends: 2 × 0.04 × 0.08 = 0.006 m²
- **Armrest SA: 0.090 m²**

*Outer Side Panel (row-end seats only — averaged across all seats):*
- Exposed side panel per end seat: 0.95 m deep × 0.80 m tall = 0.760 m²
- Row-end seats: 94 total (2 per row × 47 rows); 1 exposed panel each
- Averaged across 490 seats: (94 × 0.760) / 490 = 71.44 / 490 = 0.146 m² per seat average
- **Outer Panel SA: 0.146 m²**

*Steel Pedestals (2 per seat, round hollow tube):*
- Lateral surface per pedestal: π × 0.06 × 0.40 = 0.0754 m²
- Top and base caps (2 × 2): 4 × π × 0.030² = 0.011 m²
- Both pedestals: 2 × 0.0754 + 0.011 = **0.162 m²**

*Under-Seat Structural Connecting Bar (1 per seat, rectangular hollow section):*
- 0.44 m long × 0.06 m tall × 0.03 m depth
- 2 × (0.44 × 0.06 + 0.44 × 0.03 + 0.06 × 0.03) = 2 × (0.0264 + 0.0132 + 0.0018) = **0.083 m²**

**Total SA per Seat: 0.397 + 0.519 + 0.090 + 0.146 + 0.162 + 0.083 = 1.397 m²**

**Mass per Seat:**
- Steel frame (tube pedestals + connecting bars + folding hinge bracket): 4.5 kg
- Polyurethane foam (seat pan 55 mm + back 45 mm, premium-grade):
  - Seat pan: 0.44 × 0.44 × 0.055 × 35 = 0.37 kg
  - Back: 0.44 × 0.58 × 0.045 × 35 = 0.40 kg
  - Armrest foam: 0.13 kg
  - Subtotal with density variation allowance: 1.10 kg foam; use **1.8 kg** (accounts for higher-density comfort foam used in premium performing arts seats — 40–50 kg/m³ vs 35 kg/m³ nominal)
- Velvet/premium fabric upholstery (seat, back, armrests, both faces): 0.75 kg
- Solid hardwood armrest caps: 1.4 kg
- Spring mechanism, pivot hardware, seat-number placard: 1.0 kg
- **Total Mass per Seat: 4.5 + 1.8 + 0.75 + 1.4 + 1.0 = 9.45 kg**

**Per Floor Area (490 seats in 350 m²):**
- Surface Area: (490 × 1.397) / 350 = 684.53 / 350 = **1.956 m²/m²**
- Mass: (490 × 9.45) / 350 = 4,630.5 / 350 = **13.230 kg/m²**

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Material Breakdown by Mass:**

*Steel (seat frames, folding mechanisms, spring hardware, row standards, handrails, pit rail, console/rack chassis):*
- Seat frame (pedestals, bars, hinge brackets): 4.5 × 490 / 350 = 6.300 kg/m²
- Spring mechanism and hardware: 1.0 × 490 / 350 = 1.400 kg/m²
- Row end standards: 1.217 kg/m²
- Aisle handrails: 0.686 kg/m²
- Orchestra pit barrier rail: 0.094 kg/m²
- Sound console and rack chassis (steel/aluminum): 0.314 kg/m²
- **Total steel/aluminum: 10.011 kg/m²** (64.1%)

*Polyurethane foam (seat and back cushioning):*
- 1.8 × 490 / 350 = **2.520 kg/m²** (16.1%)

*Fabric/velvet upholstery (seat, back, armrests):*
- 0.75 × 490 / 350 = **1.050 kg/m²** (6.7%)

*Solid hardwood (armrest caps):*
- 1.4 × 490 / 350 = **1.960 kg/m²** (12.6%)

*Electronics/plastic components (rack panels, console inserts):*
- 0.086 kg/m² (0.6%)

**Total: 10.011 + 2.520 + 1.050 + 1.960 + 0.086 = 15.627 kg/m²** ✓

### Volume Fractions (for Conductivity Weighting)

```
V_i = mass_i / density_i  [m³ per m² of floor area]

Steel/Al:  10.011 / 7,800  = 0.001284 m³/m²
Foam:       2.520 /    35  = 0.072000 m³/m²
Fabric:     1.050 /   550  = 0.001909 m³/m²
Hardwood:   1.960 /   700  = 0.002800 m³/m²
Plastic:    0.086 / 1,200  = 0.000072 m³/m²

V_total = 0.001284 + 0.072000 + 0.001909 + 0.002800 + 0.000072 = 0.078065 m³/m²

Volume fractions:
  Steel/Al:  0.001284 / 0.078065 = 1.644%
  Foam:      0.072000 / 0.078065 = 92.23%
  Fabric:    0.001909 / 0.078065 = 2.445%
  Hardwood:  0.002800 / 0.078065 = 3.587%
  Plastic:   0.000072 / 0.078065 = 0.092%
```

> Polyurethane foam occupies 92.2% of composite volume despite contributing only 16.1% of composite mass — an even more extreme foam dominance than the large-format auditorium seating (91.5%). The thicker foam cushions used in premium performing arts theater seats (55 mm seat, 45 mm back vs. 50 mm/40 mm in the auditorium) increase the foam volume fraction slightly while also raising the specific heat of the composite. Steel, despite representing 64.1% of the mass, occupies only 1.6% of the volume.

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Total mass / Total volume
            = 15.627 / 0.078065
            = 200.2 kg/m³  →  200 kg/m³
```

> The composite density of 200 kg/m³ is even lower than the large-format auditorium seating type (219 kg/m³). Two factors combine: (1) the lower seat density (1.40 seats/m² vs. 1.50) reduces steel frame mass per floor area; (2) thicker foam cushions increase foam volume per seat. The result is a slightly larger foam-dominated volume envelope per unit floor area. This is the lowest composite density of the audience seating space types.

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Material properties:
  Steel/Al:  460 J/kg·K   (carbon steel / aluminum, averaged ~460)
  Foam:    1,700 J/kg·K   (polyurethane foam, semi-open cell)
  Fabric:  1,340 J/kg·K   (commercial textile/velvet)
  Hardwood:1,700 J/kg·K   (solid hardwood)
  Plastic: 1,300 J/kg·K   (ABS/polycarbonate rack panels)

Steel/Al:  10.011 × 460   = 4,605
Foam:       2.520 × 1,700 = 4,284
Fabric:     1.050 × 1,340 = 1,407
Hardwood:   1.960 × 1,700 = 3,332
Plastic:    0.086 × 1,300 =   112

c_p,composite = (4,605 + 4,284 + 1,407 + 3,332 + 112) / 15.627
              = 13,740 / 15.627
              = 879.3 J/kg·K  →  879 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity (Volume-Weighted)

```
k_composite = Σ(V_frac_i × k_i)

Material conductivities:
  Steel/Al:  50.0 W/m·K   (carbon steel; aluminum ~160 W/m·K, but fraction small)
  Foam:       0.038 W/m·K (polyurethane foam, typical)
  Fabric:     0.06 W/m·K  (textile)
  Hardwood:   0.15 W/m·K  (hardwood, across grain)
  Plastic:    0.25 W/m·K  (ABS/polycarbonate)

Steel/Al:  0.01644 × 50.0  = 0.822
Foam:      0.92230 × 0.038 = 0.035
Fabric:    0.02445 × 0.06  = 0.001
Hardwood:  0.03587 × 0.15  = 0.005
Plastic:   0.00092 × 0.25  = 0.000

k_composite ≈ 0.822 + 0.035 + 0.001 + 0.005
            ≈ 0.863 W/m·K
```

> As with the large-format auditorium, steel dominates composite conductivity despite its tiny volume fraction (1.6%), contributing 0.822 W/m·K (95.2% of total). Foam at 92.2% of volume contributes only 0.035 W/m·K. The slightly lower conductivity than the auditorium (0.863 vs. 0.966 W/m·K) results from the reduced steel volume fraction — fewer seats per m² means fewer steel pedestals per m².

### Effective Thickness

```
t_eff = Total mass per m² / (SA_ratio × composite density)
      = 15.627 / (2.06 × 200)
      = 15.627 / 412.0
      = 0.03793 m  ≈  0.038 m  (38 mm)
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 200 × 879
    = 175,800 J/m³·K
```
