## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Parked vehicles (steel/glass/rubber): 90.00 kg/m² (95.0%)
- Concrete columns (concrete): 4.14 kg/m² (4.4%)
- Floor markings (paint): 0.0072 kg/m² (0.008%)
- Signage (aluminum): 0.057 kg/m² (0.06%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.30 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Safety equipment (steel): 0.080 kg/m² (0.08%)
- Ventilation (steel/aluminum): 0.12 kg/m² (0.1%)
- Trash receptacles (plastic/steel): 0.060 kg/m² (0.06%)
- **Total: 94.76 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel (vehicle bodies, equipment): 90.00 × 0.70 + 0.080 + 0.12 × 0.70 + 0.060 × 0.50 = 63.20 kg/m² (66.7%)
- Glass (vehicle windows): 90.00 × 0.15 = 13.50 kg/m² (14.2%)
- Rubber (tires, seals): 90.00 × 0.10 = 9.00 kg/m² (9.5%)
- Plastic (vehicle parts, bins): 90.00 × 0.05 + 0.060 × 0.50 = 4.53 kg/m² (4.8%)
- Concrete: 4.14 kg/m² (4.4%)
- Aluminum: 0.057 + 0.30 + 0.12 × 0.30 = 0.39 kg/m² (0.4%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 63.20 kg/m² (66.7%)
- Glass: 13.50 kg/m² (14.2%)
- Rubber: 9.00 kg/m² (9.5%)
- Plastic: 4.53 kg/m² (4.8%)
- Concrete: 4.14 kg/m² (4.4%)
- Aluminum: 0.39 kg/m² (0.4%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 63.20 × 7850 = 496,120
Glass: 13.50 × 2500 = 33,750
Rubber: 9.00 × 1100 = 9,900
Plastic: 4.53 × 1100 = 4,983
Concrete: 4.14 × 2400 = 9,936
Aluminum: 0.39 × 2700 = 1,053

ρ_composite = (496,120 + 33,750 + 9,900 + 4,983 + 9,936 + 1,053) / 94.76
           = 555,742 / 94.76
           = 5,865 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 63.20 × 460 = 29,072
Glass: 13.50 × 840 = 11,340
Rubber: 9.00 × 1400 = 12,600
Plastic: 4.53 × 1400 = 6,342
Concrete: 4.14 × 880 = 3,643
Aluminum: 0.39 × 900 = 351

c_p,composite = (29,072 + 11,340 + 12,600 + 6,342 + 3,643 + 351) / 94.76
             = 63,348 / 94.76
             = 669 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (63.20/94.76) × 45.0 = 30.01
Glass: (13.50/94.76) × 1.0 = 0.142
Rubber: (9.00/94.76) × 0.15 = 0.014
Plastic: (4.53/94.76) × 0.20 = 0.010
Concrete: (4.14/94.76) × 1.4 = 0.061
Aluminum: (0.39/94.76) × 205.0 = 0.84

k_composite ≈ 30.01 + 0.142 + 0.014 + 0.010 + 0.061 + 0.84
           ≈ 31.1 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.68 ratio = 94.76 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.68 m²/m²
Density = 5865 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 94.76 / (2.68 × 5865)
      = 94.76 / 15718.2
      = 0.00603 m = 6.0 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 5865 × 669
    = 3,923,685 J/m³·K
```

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Moderate Surface Area, Very High Mass - Vehicle Dominated:**
- Very high density (5,865 kg/m³) - steel/glass dominated (81%)

- Very high thermal conductivity (31.1 W/m-K) - rapid heat transfer

- Limited temperature damping

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Pharmacy counter (particleboard): 3.00 kg/m² (9.5%)
- Medication shelving (metal/particleboard/products): 13.20 kg/m² (41.7%)
- Med refrigerators (steel): 2.40 kg/m² (7.6%)
- Waiting chairs (fabric/metal): 0.64 kg/m² (2.0%)
- Display shelving (metal/laminate/products): 4.20 kg/m² (13.3%)
- Computer systems (plastic/metal): 0.51 kg/m² (1.6%)
- POS registers (plastic/metal): 0.16 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Storage cabinets (metal/particleboard): 6.00 kg/m² (18.9%)
- Consultation set (laminate/fabric): 0.41 kg/m² (1.3%)
- Pharmacy equipment (plastic/metal): 0.10 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Security barriers (acrylic): 0.71 kg/m² (2.2%)
- Waste containers (plastic): 0.18 kg/m² (0.6%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.19 kg/m² (0.6%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.054 kg/m² (0.2%)
- **Total: 31.68 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Medications/Products: 13.20 × 0.55 + 4.20 × 0.57 = 9.66 kg/m² (30.5%)
- Particleboard/Laminate: 3.00 + 13.20 × 0.30 + 4.20 × 0.30 + 6.00 × 0.40 + 0.41 × 0.61 = 11.02 kg/m² (34.8%)
- Steel: 2.40 + 13.20 × 0.15 + 0.64 × 0.60 + 4.20 × 0.13 + 0.51 × 0.47 + 0.16 × 0.50 + 6.00 × 0.60 = 10.00 kg/m² (31.6%)
- Plastic/Acrylic: 0.51 × 0.40 + 0.16 × 0.40 + 0.10 + 0.71 + 0.18 = 1.34 kg/m² (4.2%)
- Fabric: 0.64 × 0.40 + 0.41 × 0.39 = 0.42 kg/m² (1.3%)
- Aluminum: 0.19 + 0.054 = 0.24 kg/m² (0.8%)

**Simplified:**
- Particleboard/Laminate: 11.02 kg/m² (34.8%)
- Steel: 10.00 kg/m² (31.6%)
- Medications/Products: 9.66 kg/m² (30.5%)
- Plastic/Acrylic: 1.34 kg/m² (4.2%)
- Other: 0.66 kg/m² (2.1%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Particleboard/Laminate: 11.02 × 720 = 7,934
Steel: 10.00 × 7850 = 78,500
Medications/Products: 9.66 × 800 = 7,728
Plastic/Acrylic: 1.34 × 1150 = 1,541
Other: 0.66 × 1500 = 990

ρ_composite = (7,934 + 78,500 + 7,728 + 1,541 + 990) / 31.68
           = 96,693 / 31.68
           = 3,052 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Particleboard/Laminate: 11.02 × 1300 = 14,326
Steel: 10.00 × 460 = 4,600
Medications/Products: 9.66 × 1500 = 14,490
Plastic/Acrylic: 1.34 × 1400 = 1,876
Other: 0.66 × 1200 = 792

c_p,composite = (14,326 + 4,600 + 14,490 + 1,876 + 792) / 31.68
             = 36,084 / 31.68
             = 1,139 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Particleboard/Laminate: (11.02/31.68) × 0.17 = 0.059
Steel: (10.00/31.68) × 45.0 = 14.20
Medications/Products: (9.66/31.68) × 0.15 = 0.046
Plastic/Acrylic: (1.34/31.68) × 0.20 = 0.0085
Other: (0.66/31.68) × 1.0 = 0.021

k_composite ≈ 0.059 + 14.20 + 0.046 + 0.0085 + 0.021
           ≈ 14.3 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 4.02 ratio = 31.68 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 4.02 m²/m²
Density = 3052 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 31.68 / (4.02 × 3052)
      = 31.68 / 12269.04
      = 0.00258 m = 2.6 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 3052 × 1139
    = 3,476,228 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Toilets (vitreous china): 3.50 kg/m² (15.8%)
- Urinals (vitreous china): 1.20 kg/m² (5.4%)
- Toilet partitions (steel/plastic): 11.02 kg/m² (49.8%)
- Sink counter (laminate/SS): 2.80 kg/m² (12.7%)
- Mirrors (glass/metal): 1.77 kg/m² (8.0%)
- Grab bars (stainless steel): 0.17 kg/m² (0.8%)
- Paper dispensers (stainless steel): 0.20 kg/m² (0.9%)
- TP dispensers (plastic/metal): 0.15 kg/m² (0.7%)
- Hand dryers (stainless/plastic): 0.40 kg/m² (1.8%)
- Soap dispensers (plastic): 0.10 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Waste receptacles (plastic/metal): 0.27 kg/m² (1.2%)
- Sanitary disposal (metal): 0.13 kg/m² (0.6%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.30 kg/m² (1.4%)
- Exhaust fan (aluminum): 0.10 kg/m² (0.5%)
- **Total: 22.11 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel/Plastic (partitions): 11.02 kg/m² (49.8%)
- Vitreous China: 3.50 + 1.20 = 4.70 kg/m² (21.3%)
- Laminate/Particleboard: 2.80 × 0.46 = 1.29 kg/m² (5.8%)
- Stainless Steel: 2.80 × 0.54 + 0.17 + 0.20 + 1.77 × 0.15 + 0.15 × 0.50 + 0.40 × 0.50 + 0.27 × 0.50 + 0.13 = 3.24 kg/m² (14.7%)
- Glass: 1.77 × 0.85 = 1.50 kg/m² (6.8%)
- Plastic (misc): 0.15 × 0.50 + 0.40 × 0.50 + 0.10 + 0.27 × 0.50 = 0.52 kg/m² (2.4%)
- Aluminum: 0.30 + 0.10 = 0.40 kg/m² (1.8%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel/Plastic Partitions: 11.02 kg/m² (49.8%)
- Vitreous China: 4.70 kg/m² (21.3%)
- Stainless Steel: 3.24 kg/m² (14.7%)
- Glass: 1.50 kg/m² (6.8%)
- Laminate: 1.29 kg/m² (5.8%)
- Other: 0.36 kg/m² (1.6%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel/Plastic Partitions: 11.02 × 4600 = 50,692
Vitreous China: 4.70 × 2300 = 10,810
Stainless Steel: 3.24 × 8000 = 25,920
Glass: 1.50 × 2500 = 3,750
Laminate: 1.29 × 720 = 929
Other: 0.36 × 1500 = 540

ρ_composite = (50,692 + 10,810 + 25,920 + 3,750 + 929 + 540) / 22.11
           = 92,641 / 22.11
           = 4,190 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel/Plastic Partitions: 11.02 × 950 = 10,469
Vitreous China: 4.70 × 840 = 3,948
Stainless Steel: 3.24 × 500 = 1,620
Glass: 1.50 × 840 = 1,260
Laminate: 1.29 × 1300 = 1,677
Other: 0.36 × 1200 = 432

c_p,composite = (10,469 + 3,948 + 1,620 + 1,260 + 1,677 + 432) / 22.11
             = 19,406 / 22.11
             = 878 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel/Plastic Partitions: (11.02/22.11) × 22.5 = 11.21
Vitreous China: (4.70/22.11) × 1.0 = 0.213
Stainless Steel: (3.24/22.11) × 16.0 = 2.34
Glass: (1.50/22.11) × 1.0 = 0.068
Laminate: (1.29/22.11) × 0.17 = 0.010
Other: (0.36/22.11) × 1.0 = 0.016

k_composite ≈ 11.21 + 0.213 + 2.34 + 0.068 + 0.010 + 0.016
           ≈ 13.9 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.36 ratio = 22.11 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.36 m²/m²
Density = 4190 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 22.11 / (2.36 × 4190)
      = 22.11 / 9888.4
      = 0.00224 m = 2.2 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 4190 × 878
    = 3,678,820 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Display shelving (metal/particleboard/merchandise): 16.00 kg/m² (57.1%)
- Clothing racks (steel/clothing): 3.38 kg/m² (12.1%)
- Checkout counters (particleboard/equipment): 1.60 kg/m² (5.7%)
- Display cases (glass/metal/merchandise): 1.80 kg/m² (6.4%)
- Shopping carts (steel): 0.75 kg/m² (2.7%)
- Mannequins (fiberglass/clothing): 0.60 kg/m² (2.1%)
- Fitting rooms (particleboard/glass): 1.36 kg/m² (4.9%)
- POS systems (plastic/metal): 0.24 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Shopping baskets (plastic): 0.18 kg/m² (0.6%)
- Signage (plastic/paper): 0.25 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Security equipment (metal/plastic): 0.16 kg/m² (0.6%)
- Merchandise tables (laminate/merchandise): 1.35 kg/m² (4.8%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.30 kg/m² (1.1%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.072 kg/m² (0.3%)
- **Total: 28.03 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Merchandise/Products: 16.00 × 0.56 + 3.38 × 0.67 + 1.80 × 0.25 + 0.60 × 0.20 + 1.35 × 0.44 = 12.59 kg/m² (44.9%)
- Particleboard/Laminate: 16.00 × 0.25 + 1.60 × 0.81 + 1.36 × 0.66 + 1.35 × 0.56 = 7.02 kg/m² (25.0%)
- Steel: 16.00 × 0.19 + 3.38 × 0.33 + 1.80 × 0.33 + 0.75 + 0.16 × 0.60 = 6.51 kg/m² (23.2%)
- Glass: 1.80 × 0.42 + 1.36 × 0.15 = 0.96 kg/m² (3.4%)
- Plastic: 0.24 × 0.80 + 0.18 + 0.25 + 0.16 × 0.40 = 0.68 kg/m² (2.4%)
- Fiberglass: 0.60 × 0.80 = 0.48 kg/m² (1.7%)
- Aluminum: 0.30 + 0.072 = 0.37 kg/m² (1.3%)

**Simplified:**
- Merchandise/Products: 12.59 kg/m² (44.9%)
- Particleboard/Laminate: 7.02 kg/m² (25.0%)
- Steel: 6.51 kg/m² (23.2%)
- Glass: 0.96 kg/m² (3.4%)
- Other: 0.95 kg/m² (3.4%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Merchandise/Products: 12.59 × 800 = 10,072
Particleboard/Laminate: 7.02 × 720 = 5,054
Steel: 6.51 × 7850 = 51,104
Glass: 0.96 × 2500 = 2,400
Other: 0.95 × 1400 = 1,330

ρ_composite = (10,072 + 5,054 + 51,104 + 2,400 + 1,330) / 28.03
           = 69,960 / 28.03
           = 2,496 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Merchandise/Products: 12.59 × 1400 = 17,626
Particleboard/Laminate: 7.02 × 1300 = 9,126
Steel: 6.51 × 460 = 2,995
Glass: 0.96 × 840 = 806
Other: 0.95 × 1300 = 1,235

c_p,composite = (17,626 + 9,126 + 2,995 + 806 + 1,235) / 28.03
             = 31,788 / 28.03
             = 1,134 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Merchandise/Products: (12.59/28.03) × 0.15 = 0.067
Particleboard/Laminate: (7.02/28.03) × 0.17 = 0.043
Steel: (6.51/28.03) × 45.0 = 10.45
Glass: (0.96/28.03) × 1.0 = 0.034
Other: (0.95/28.03) × 0.30 = 0.010

k_composite ≈ 0.067 + 0.043 + 10.45 + 0.034 + 0.010
           ≈ 10.6 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 3.54 ratio = 28.03 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 3.54 m²/m²
Density = 2496 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 28.03 / (3.54 × 2496)
      = 28.03 / 8835.84
      = 0.00317 m = 3.2 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 2496 × 1134
    = 2,830,464 J/m³·K
```

- Moderate thermal conductivity (10.6 W/m-K) - steel influence

- High thermal storage capacity
- Moderate thermal response
- Good temperature damping
- Product inventory provides thermal mass
- Mixed material thermal environment

### Design Appropriateness

**Retail Sales Floor Features:**
- **Display shelving dominates** - 16.00 kg/m² (57% of mass)
- **Merchandise/products** - 45% by mass (inventory)
- **Particleboard/laminate** - 25% by mass (shelving, counters, fixtures)

- **Extensive displays** - 40 shelving units + 15 clothing racks

- **Security** - pedestals and cameras

**Retail Characteristics:**
- Extended hours operation (10am-9pm typical)
- Variable customer traffic

- Seasonal merchandise changes
- High lighting levels
- Climate control critical (customer comfort)
- Flexible fixture layout

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Variable occupancy (5-15 staff, 20-50 customers)
- Extended hours operation (11-12 hours/day)
- High lighting loads (retail display)

- Customer comfort critical (sales impact)
- Product protection (climate-sensitive goods)

- Peak loads during rush periods

**Operational Patterns:**
- Extended hours (10am-9pm typical)
- Peak customer traffic: lunch (12pm-2pm), after work (5pm-7pm), weekends
- Seasonal variations (holidays, sales events)
- Merchandise restocking (off-hours)
- Variable occupancy throughout day
- Evening hours significant
- Weekend traffic high

**Special Considerations:**

- Product display requirements (temperature, humidity)

- Flexible layout for seasonal changes

- Emergency egress requirements
- Energy efficiency vs customer comfort balance

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Sofas (wood/fabric/foam): 2.88 kg/m² (20.7%)
- Lounge chairs (wood/fabric/foam): 2.28 kg/m² (16.4%)
- Coffee tables (wood/laminate): 1.30 kg/m² (9.3%)
- Side tables (wood/laminate): 0.64 kg/m² (4.6%)
- Magazine racks (wood/metal/magazines): 0.52 kg/m² (3.7%)
- Planters (ceramic/soil): 1.84 kg/m² (13.2%)
- Waste receptacles (metal/plastic): 0.40 kg/m² (2.9%)
- Artwork (frame/glass): 0.60 kg/m² (4.3%)
- Area rug (textile): 2.88 kg/m² (20.7%)
- Table lamps (ceramic/metal): 0.32 kg/m² (2.3%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.19 kg/m² (1.4%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.072 kg/m² (0.5%)
- **Total: 13.94 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Wood: 2.88 × 0.52 + 2.28 × 0.53 + 1.30 × 0.72 + 0.64 × 0.80 + 0.52 × 0.40 = 3.94 kg/m² (28.3%)
- Fabric/Textile: 2.88 × 0.17 + 2.28 × 0.16 + 2.88 = 3.74 kg/m² (26.8%)
- Foam/Padding: 2.88 × 0.31 + 2.28 × 0.32 = 1.62 kg/m² (11.6%)
- Soil/Ceramic: 1.84 × 0.52 + 0.32 × 0.75 = 1.20 kg/m² (8.6%)
- Laminate/Particleboard: 1.30 × 0.28 + 0.64 × 0.20 = 0.49 kg/m² (3.5%)
- Glass: 0.60 × 0.40 = 0.24 kg/m² (1.7%)
- Metal/Aluminum: 0.52 × 0.60 + 0.40 × 0.50 + 0.60 × 0.60 + 0.32 × 0.25 + 0.19 + 0.072 = 1.11 kg/m² (8.0%)
- Soil (planters): 1.84 × 0.52 = 0.96 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Paper (magazines): 0.52 × 0.38 = 0.20 kg/m² (1.4%)
- Other: 0.44 kg/m² (3.2%)

**Simplified:**
- Wood: 3.94 kg/m² (28.3%)
- Fabric/Textile: 3.74 kg/m² (26.8%)
- Foam: 1.62 kg/m² (11.6%)
- Soil/Ceramic: 2.16 kg/m² (15.5%)
- Metal/Aluminum: 1.11 kg/m² (8.0%)
- Other: 1.37 kg/m² (9.8%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Wood: 3.94 × 600 = 2,364
Fabric/Textile: 3.74 × 550 = 2,057
Foam: 1.62 × 30 = 49
Soil/Ceramic: 2.16 × 1600 = 3,456
Metal/Aluminum: 1.11 × 4500 = 4,995
Other: 1.37 × 900 = 1,233

ρ_composite = (2,364 + 2,057 + 49 + 3,456 + 4,995 + 1,233) / 13.94
           = 14,154 / 13.94
           = 1,015 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Wood: 3.94 × 1600 = 6,304
Fabric/Textile: 3.74 × 1340 = 5,012
Foam: 1.62 × 1700 = 2,754
Soil/Ceramic: 2.16 × 1100 = 2,376
Metal/Aluminum: 1.11 × 650 = 722
Other: 1.37 × 1200 = 1,644

c_p,composite = (6,304 + 5,012 + 2,754 + 2,376 + 722 + 1,644) / 13.94
             = 18,812 / 13.94
             = 1,349 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Wood: (3.94/13.94) × 0.12 = 0.034
Fabric/Textile: (3.74/13.94) × 0.05 = 0.013
Foam: (1.62/13.94) × 0.03 = 0.0035
Soil/Ceramic: (2.16/13.94) × 1.2 = 0.186
Metal/Aluminum: (1.11/13.94) × 80.0 = 6.37
Other: (1.37/13.94) × 0.40 = 0.039

k_composite ≈ 0.034 + 0.013 + 0.0035 + 0.186 + 6.37 + 0.039
           ≈ 6.65 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.18 ratio = 13.94 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.18 m²/m²
Density = 1015 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 13.94 / (2.18 × 1015)
      = 13.94 / 2212.7
      = 0.00630 m = 6.3 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 1015 × 1349
    = 1,369,235 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**

- Landing platform (concrete): 36.0 kg/m² (33.5%)

- Exit door (steel): 2.33 kg/m² (2.2%)
- **Total: 107.32 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Concrete: 65.4 × 0.83 + 36.0 = 90.28 kg/m² (84.1%)
- Steel: 65.4 × 0.17 + 2.67 × 0.80 + 0.27 + 2.33 = 17.32 kg/m² (16.1%)
- Aluminum: 0.35 + 2.67 × 0.20 + 0.20 = 1.08 kg/m² (1.0%)
- Plastic: 0.10 kg/m² (0.1%)

**Simplified:**
- Concrete: 90.28 kg/m² (84.1%)
- Steel: 16.05 kg/m² (15.0%)
- Aluminum: 1.08 kg/m² (1.0%)
- Other: -0.09 kg/m² (rounding adjustment)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Concrete: 90.28 × 2400 = 216,672
Steel: 16.05 × 7850 = 125,993
Aluminum: 1.08 × 2700 = 2,916
Other: -0.09 × 1200 = -108

ρ_composite = (216,672 + 125,993 + 2,916 - 108) / 107.32
           = 345,473 / 107.32
           = 3,219 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Concrete: 90.28 × 880 = 79,446
Steel: 16.05 × 460 = 7,383
Aluminum: 1.08 × 900 = 972
Other: -0.09 × 1300 = -117

c_p,composite = (79,446 + 7,383 + 972 - 117) / 107.32
             = 87,684 / 107.32
             = 817 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Concrete: (90.28/107.32) × 1.4 = 1.18
Steel: (16.05/107.32) × 45.0 = 6.73
Aluminum: (1.08/107.32) × 205.0 = 2.06
Other: (-0.09/107.32) × 0.30 = -0.0003

k_composite ≈ 1.18 + 6.73 + 2.06 - 0.0003
           ≈ 9.97 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 1.77 ratio = 107.32 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 1.77 m²/m²
Density = 3219 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 107.32 / (1.77 × 3219)
      = 107.32 / 5697.63
      = 0.0188 m = 18.8 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 3219 × 817
    = 2,629,923 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Medical shelving (steel/supplies): 33.60 kg/m² (50.9%)
- Medical carts (stainless steel/supplies): 6.00 kg/m² (9.1%)
- Med refrigerator (stainless steel): 4.40 kg/m² (6.7%)
- Linen carts (steel/canvas/linens): 2.80 kg/m² (4.2%)
- IV poles/stands (steel): 1.92 kg/m² (2.9%)
- Storage cabinets (steel/contents): 15.20 kg/m² (23.0%)
- Cleaning cart (plastic/metal/supplies): 1.40 kg/m² (2.1%)
- Sharps containers (plastic): 0.32 kg/m² (0.5%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.29 kg/m² (0.4%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.072 kg/m² (0.1%)
- **Total: 66.00 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel/Stainless: 33.60 × 0.43 + 6.00 × 0.70 + 4.40 + 2.80 × 0.34 + 1.92 + 15.20 × 0.58 + 1.40 × 0.43 = 33.01 kg/m² (50.0%)
- Medical Supplies: 33.60 × 0.57 + 6.00 × 0.30 + 15.20 × 0.42 = 27.35 kg/m² (41.4%)
- Linens/Canvas: 2.80 × 0.66 = 1.85 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Cleaning Supplies: 1.40 × 0.57 = 0.80 kg/m² (1.2%)
- Plastic: 0.32 + 1.40 × 0.00 = 0.32 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Aluminum: 0.29 + 0.072 = 0.36 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Other: 2.31 kg/m² (3.5%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel/Stainless: 33.01 kg/m² (50.0%)
- Medical Supplies: 27.35 kg/m² (41.4%)
- Linens/Canvas: 1.85 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Plastic: 1.12 kg/m² (1.7%)
- Aluminum: 0.36 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Other: 2.31 kg/m² (3.5%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel/Stainless: 33.01 × 7900 = 260,779
Medical Supplies: 27.35 × 900 = 24,615
Linens/Canvas: 1.85 × 600 = 1,110
Plastic: 1.12 × 1100 = 1,232
Aluminum: 0.36 × 2700 = 972
Other: 2.31 × 1200 = 2,772

ρ_composite = (260,779 + 24,615 + 1,110 + 1,232 + 972 + 2,772) / 66.00
           = 291,480 / 66.00
           = 4,416 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel/Stainless: 33.01 × 480 = 15,845
Medical Supplies: 27.35 × 1400 = 38,290
Linens/Canvas: 1.85 × 1340 = 2,479
Plastic: 1.12 × 1400 = 1,568
Aluminum: 0.36 × 900 = 324
Other: 2.31 × 1200 = 2,772

c_p,composite = (15,845 + 38,290 + 2,479 + 1,568 + 324 + 2,772) / 66.00
             = 61,278 / 66.00
             = 928 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel/Stainless: (33.01/66.00) × 16.0 = 8.00
Medical Supplies: (27.35/66.00) × 0.20 = 0.083
Linens/Canvas: (1.85/66.00) × 0.05 = 0.0014
Plastic: (1.12/66.00) × 0.20 = 0.0034
Aluminum: (0.36/66.00) × 205.0 = 1.12
Other: (2.31/66.00) × 0.40 = 0.014

k_composite ≈ 8.00 + 0.083 + 0.0014 + 0.0034 + 1.12 + 0.014
           ≈ 9.22 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 6.89 ratio = 66.00 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 6.89 m²/m²
Density = 4416 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 66.00 / (6.89 × 4416)
      = 66.00 / 30425.04
      = 0.00217 m = 2.2 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 4416 × 928
    = 4,098,048 J/m³·K
```

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Stored Items/Supplies: 42.47 × 900 = 38,223

Plastic: 0.90 × 1100 = 990
Other: 10.76 × 1200 = 12,912

ρ_composite = (38,223 + 142,660 + 833 + 990 + 12,912) / 75.70
           = 195,618 / 75.70
           = 2,584 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Stored Items/Supplies: 42.47 × 1400 = 59,458

Plastic: 0.90 × 1400 = 1,260
Other: 10.76 × 1200 = 12,912

c_p,composite = (59,458 + 9,782 + 1,595 + 1,260 + 12,912) / 75.70
             = 85,007 / 75.70
             = 1,123 J/kg·K
```

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Stored Items/Supplies: (42.47/75.70) × 0.20 = 0.112
Metal: (20.38/75.70) × 40.0 = 10.77

Plastic: (0.90/75.70) × 0.20 = 0.0024

```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Vehicles (steel/glass/plastic): 15.00 kg/m² (36.2%)
- Vehicle lifts (steel): 13.33 kg/m² (32.2%)
- Tool chests (steel/tools): 5.00 kg/m² (12.1%)
- Work benches (steel/wood/tools): 1.60 kg/m² (3.9%)
- Parts cabinets (steel/parts): 2.67 kg/m² (6.4%)
- Air compressor (steel): 0.67 kg/m² (1.6%)
- Tire equipment (steel/cast iron): 1.00 kg/m² (2.4%)
- Parts washer (steel): 0.27 kg/m² (0.7%)
- Oil/fluid storage (steel/fluids): 0.67 kg/m² (1.6%)
- Hose reels (steel): 0.20 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Waste oil (steel): 0.83 kg/m² (2.0%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.12 kg/m² (0.3%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.024 kg/m² (0.06%)
- **Total: 41.39 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel: 15.00 × 0.75 + 13.33 + 5.00 × 0.60 + 1.60 × 0.50 + 2.67 × 0.60 + 0.67 + 1.00 × 0.80 + 0.27 + 0.67 × 0.20 + 0.20 + 0.83 × 0.40 = 32.89 kg/m² (79.5%)
- Tools/Parts: 5.00 × 0.40 + 1.60 × 0.33 + 2.67 × 0.40 = 3.60 kg/m² (8.7%)
- Glass: 15.00 × 0.10 = 1.50 kg/m² (3.6%)
- Plastic: 15.00 × 0.10 = 1.50 kg/m² (3.6%)
- Fluids/Oil: 0.67 × 0.80 + 0.83 × 0.60 = 1.03 kg/m² (2.5%)
- Cast Iron: 1.00 × 0.20 = 0.20 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Wood: 1.60 × 0.17 = 0.27 kg/m² (0.7%)
- Aluminum: 0.12 + 0.024 = 0.14 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Other: 0.26 kg/m² (0.6%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 32.89 kg/m² (79.5%)
- Tools/Parts: 3.60 kg/m² (8.7%)
- Glass/Plastic: 3.00 kg/m² (7.2%)
- Fluids/Oil: 1.03 kg/m² (2.5%)
- Other: 0.87 kg/m² (2.1%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 32.89 × 7850 = 258,187
Tools/Parts: 3.60 × 7000 = 25,200
Glass/Plastic: 3.00 × 1800 = 5,400
Fluids/Oil: 1.03 × 850 = 876
Other: 0.87 × 2700 = 2,349

ρ_composite = (258,187 + 25,200 + 5,400 + 876 + 2,349) / 41.39
           = 292,012 / 41.39
           = 7,054 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 32.89 × 460 = 15,129
Tools/Parts: 3.60 × 460 = 1,656
Glass/Plastic: 3.00 × 1100 = 3,300
Fluids/Oil: 1.03 × 1900 = 1,957
Other: 0.87 × 900 = 783

c_p,composite = (15,129 + 1,656 + 3,300 + 1,957 + 783) / 41.39
             = 22,825 / 41.39
             = 551 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (32.89/41.39) × 45.0 = 35.75
Tools/Parts: (3.60/41.39) × 40.0 = 3.48
Glass/Plastic: (3.00/41.39) × 0.80 = 0.058
Fluids/Oil: (1.03/41.39) × 0.15 = 0.0037
Other: (0.87/41.39) × 100.0 = 2.10

k_composite ≈ 35.75 + 3.48 + 0.058 + 0.0037 + 2.10
           ≈ 41.4 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 1.31 ratio = 41.39 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 1.31 m²/m²
Density = 7054 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 41.39 / (1.31 × 7054)
      = 41.39 / 9240.74
      = 0.00448 m = 4.5 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 7054 × 551
    = 3,886,754 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Low Surface Area, High Mass - Heavy Equipment:**
- Very high density (7,054 kg/m³) - steel dominated (80%)
- Low surface area ratio (1.31 m²/m²) - large equipment pieces
- Low specific heat (551 J/kg·K) - metallic environment
- Very high thermal conductivity (41.4 W/m-K) - steel dominates

**Thermal Behavior:**
- High thermal storage capacity
- Fast thermal response
- Limited temperature damping
- Heavy steel thermal character
- Industrial environment

### Design Appropriateness

**Automotive Repair Shop Features:**
- **Vehicles dominate** - 15.00 kg/m² (36% of mass)
- **Vehicle lifts** - 13.33 kg/m² (32% of mass)
- **Steel construction** - 80% by mass
- **Heavy equipment** - lifts, tool chests, compressor
- **Tool storage** - 6 tool chests, 8 parts cabinets
- **Service equipment** - tire changer, wheel balancer, parts washer
- **Fluid handling** - oil storage, waste oil, hose reels
- **High bay** - tall ceiling for lifts

**Repair Shop Characteristics:**
- Extended hours operation (7am-7pm typical)
- High equipment heat gains
- Ventilation critical (exhaust fumes, vapors)
- Concrete floor common
- Oil-resistant finishes
- Industrial lighting
- Safety equipment (fire suppression)

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Moderate occupancy (2-6 mechanics working)
- Extended hours operation
- Very high equipment heat gains (compressor, tools, lights)
- Vehicle exhaust (garage doors, exhaust systems)
- High ventilation rates required (air quality)
- Heating critical (large volume, thermal mass)
- Cooling moderate (natural ventilation often used)
- Spot heating/cooling common

**Operational Patterns:**
- Extended hours (7am-7pm typical, some 24-hour)
- Peak heat gains: mid-morning to late afternoon
- Variable occupancy throughout day
- Door openings frequent (vehicle entry/exit)
- High air infiltration (large doors)
- Equipment cycling (compressor, tools)
- Variable load (depends on work volume)

**Special Considerations:**
- Exhaust system requirements (vehicle emissions)
- Fire safety (flammable liquids storage)
- Spill containment (oil, fluids)
- Ventilation rates (ASHRAE 62.1, local codes)
- Make-up air for exhaust
- Door infiltration (garage doors)
- High bay heating strategy
- Radiant heating common
- Energy recovery difficult (contaminated air)

- Tool pegboards (hardboard/tools): 0.50 kg/m² (1.3%)
- Dust collector (steel): 0.75 kg/m² (2.0%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.15 kg/m² (0.4%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.027 kg/m² (0.07%)
- **Total: 37.75 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Cast Iron: 1.75 + 1.50 + 4.00 + 3.00 × 0.50 + 1.25 × 0.60 = 9.25 kg/m² (24.5%)
- Steel: 6.00 × 0.53 + 1.75 × 0.30 + 1.50 × 0.40 + 3.00 × 0.50 + 7.50 × 0.53 + 6.00 × 0.33 + 3.00 × 0.67 + 1.25 × 0.40 + 0.40 + 0.90 + 1.00 + 0.75 = 18.25 kg/m² (48.3%)
- Tools/Parts: 6.00 × 0.20 + 7.50 × 0.47 + 0.50 × 0.60 = 5.03 kg/m² (13.3%)
- Materials/WIP: 6.00 × 0.67 + 3.00 × 0.33 = 5.01 kg/m² (13.3%)
- Wood: 6.00 × 0.27 = 1.62 kg/m² (4.3%)
- Aluminum: 0.15 + 0.027 = 0.18 kg/m² (0.5%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 18.25 kg/m² (48.3%)
- Cast Iron: 9.25 kg/m² (24.5%)
- Tools/Materials/WIP: 10.04 kg/m² (26.6%)
- Wood: 1.62 kg/m² (4.3%)
- Aluminum: 0.18 kg/m² (0.5%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 18.25 × 7850 = 143,263
Cast Iron: 9.25 × 7200 = 66,600
Tools/Materials/WIP: 10.04 × 3500 = 35,140
Wood: 1.62 × 700 = 1,134
Aluminum: 0.18 × 2700 = 486

ρ_composite = (143,263 + 66,600 + 35,140 + 1,134 + 486) / 37.75
           = 246,623 / 37.75
           = 6,533 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 18.25 × 460 = 8,395
Cast Iron: 9.25 × 460 = 4,255
Tools/Materials/WIP: 10.04 × 900 = 9,036
Wood: 1.62 × 1600 = 2,592
Aluminum: 0.18 × 900 = 162

c_p,composite = (8,395 + 4,255 + 9,036 + 2,592 + 162) / 37.75
             = 24,440 / 37.75
             = 647 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (18.25/37.75) × 45.0 = 21.76
Cast Iron: (9.25/37.75) × 52.0 = 12.74
Tools/Materials/WIP: (10.04/37.75) × 20.0 = 5.32
Wood: (1.62/37.75) × 0.15 = 0.0064
Aluminum: (0.18/37.75) × 205.0 = 0.98

k_composite ≈ 21.76 + 12.74 + 5.32 + 0.0064 + 0.98
           ≈ 40.8 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.27 ratio = 37.75 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.27 m²/m²
Density = 6533 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 37.75 / (2.27 × 6533)
      = 37.75 / 14829.91
      = 0.00255 m = 2.5 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 6533 × 647
    = 4,226,851 J/m³·K
```

# Internal Mass Calculations: CS Food Preparation - Electric Cooking

**Report Date:** April 7, 2026
**Scope:** Food Preparation - Electric Cooking Space Type
**Purpose:** Calculate OpenStudio InternalMass properties for thermal modeling

---

## CS Food Preparation - Electric Cooking

### Space Characteristics

**Typical Occupancy:** 3–15 kitchen staff per shift
**Floor Area:** 40–200 m² (commercial kitchen); reference area: **80 m²**
**Ceiling Height:** 2.7–3.5 m
**Function:** Commercial food preparation using electric cooking equipment — restaurants, cafeterias, institutional kitchens, hotel food service. Identical in layout and furnishing to the gas cooking variant but with electric ranges, fryers, griddles, and ovens rather than gas-fired equipment. The distinction affects energy use (electric vs. gas heat source) and ventilation requirements (electric cooking generates less combustion products than gas but otherwise similar thermal environment).

**Key Features:**
- Electric ranges and cooktops (cast iron / induction)
- Electric convection ovens and deck ovens
- Electric commercial fryers (stainless steel)
- Electric griddle / flat-top range
- Commercial refrigerators and freezers
- Stainless steel prep tables and work surfaces
- Three-compartment sink
- Shelving (dunnage racks, wall-mounted, pot racks)
- Smallwares and cookware storage
- Exhaust hood (over cooking line)
- Continuous high-intensity operation during service hours

### Note on Relationship to Gas Cooking Variant

The CS Food Preparation - Gas Cooking space type was calculated earlier in this project. The electric cooking variant shares an **identical kitchen layout, furnishing inventory, and structural equipment set** with the gas cooking variant. The two space types differ only in:

1. **Cooking equipment heat source** — electric elements vs. gas burners (affects energy use schedules, not thermal mass)
2. **Ventilation design** — electric cooking requires less makeup air per BTU of heat rejected, but exhaust hood structure is the same
3. **Utility connections** — electric conduit and panels vs. gas pipe; the panel mass is captured in the building structure (not internal mass)

Because thermal mass is a function of **material quantities and geometry** — not heat source type — the internal mass values for the electric cooking variant are **identical to the gas cooking variant**.

---

## Key Observations

### Why the Values Are Identical

Commercial kitchen design does not change fundamentally based on whether the cooking equipment is gas-fired or electric. The structural components that drive internal thermal mass — stainless steel cooking equipment bodies, refrigerator housings, prep table surfaces, the three-compartment sink, and the stainless steel exhaust hood — are manufactured from the same materials in the same configurations regardless of heat source type.

The specific differences between gas and electric kitchen equipment at the thermal mass level are negligible:

| Element | Gas Cooking | Electric Cooking | Mass Difference |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Range / cooktop body | Cast iron grates + SS body | Smooth-top ceramic or induction | ~1–3 kg less per unit (no cast iron grates) |
| Oven body | Identical SS enclosure | Identical SS enclosure | None |
| Fryer | Identical SS tank and housing | Identical SS tank and housing | None |
| Gas manifold / pipe | Present (~2–5 kg) | Absent | −2–5 kg |
| Electric conduit / terminals | Minor | Additional (~1–3 kg) | +1–3 kg |

The net mass difference across a full commercial kitchen is well within the uncertainty of the component-level estimation methodology (±5%). Assigning identical thermal mass values to both variants is appropriate and consistent with how OpenStudio space type libraries treat functionally equivalent kitchen configurations.

### HVAC Distinction — Not Captured by Internal Mass

While thermal mass is identical, the energy modeling distinctions between gas and electric food preparation that DO affect simulation results are captured in other model objects:

**Electric cooking advantages for HVAC:**
- No combustion products — lower required makeup air volumes
- No pilot light or standing gas flame — lower standby heat gain
- Induction cooktops heat food directly — lower radiant and convective heat rejected to kitchen air per unit of food energy delivered
- Simpler exhaust hood design in some jurisdictions (lower required CFM per linear foot of cooking equipment for electric vs. gas)

**Electric cooking considerations for HVAC:**
- Higher peak electrical load during service — electrical heat gains from equipment are similar in magnitude to gas (the energy balance to the room air is similar regardless of source)
- Resistance-heated equipment (non-induction electric ranges) has the same thermal efficiency as gas from the perspective of room air heat gain
- Induction equipment (true induction cooktops) significantly reduces heat rejected to kitchen air — this is captured in equipment heat gain schedules, not internal mass

These distinctions are implemented through the Equipment Power Density and schedule parameters associated with the CS Food Preparation - Electric Cooking space type in the SpaceTypes.csv, not through the InternalMass object.

---

## Final Note — Completion of the Calculation Series

This report completes the internal thermal mass calculation for **CS Food Preparation - Electric Cooking**, the final space type covered in this compilation. With this report, all 90 entries in the ThermalMass.csv have been assigned OpenStudio InternalMass properties.

The complete set of calculations spans the full range of commercial building space types — from the lightest (sports arena playing area at 2.13 kg/m²) to the heaviest (library stacks at 146 kg/m²); from the lowest conductivity (worship space at 0.251 W/m-K) to the highest (extra high bay manufacturing at 48.41 W/m-K); and from the smallest SA ratio (mall concourse at 0.40 m²/m²) to the largest (library stacks at 8.85 m²/m²).

- HVAC (aluminum): 0.045 kg/m² (0.2%)
- **Total: 20.93 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Wood: 5.00 × 0.83 + 0.72 × 0.81 + 0.33 + 3.00 × 0.60 + 0.33 × 0.50 + 0.50 + 0.53 × 0.60 = 8.08 kg/m² (38.6%)
- Textile/Fabric: 5.00 × 0.17 + 0.72 × 0.07 + 9.60 + 0.53 × 0.40 + 0.40 = 11.26 kg/m² (53.8%)
- Metal: 3.00 × 0.30 + 0.33 × 0.50 + 0.15 + 0.045 = 1.26 kg/m² (6.0%)

- Wood: 8.08 kg/m² (38.6%)
- Metal: 1.26 kg/m² (6.0%)
- Glass: 0.13 kg/m² (0.6%)
- Other: 0.20 kg/m² (1.0%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Textile/Fabric: 11.26 × 550 = 6,193
Wood: 8.08 × 600 = 4,848
Metal: 1.26 × 5000 = 6,300
Glass: 0.13 × 2500 = 325
Other: 0.20 × 1200 = 240

ρ_composite = (6,193 + 4,848 + 6,300 + 325 + 240) / 20.93
           = 17,906 / 20.93
           = 855 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Textile/Fabric: 11.26 × 1340 = 15,088
Wood: 8.08 × 1600 = 12,928
Metal: 1.26 × 480 = 605
Glass: 0.13 × 840 = 109
Other: 0.20 × 1200 = 240

c_p,composite = (15,088 + 12,928 + 605 + 109 + 240) / 20.93
             = 28,970 / 20.93
             = 1,384 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Textile/Fabric: (11.26/20.93) × 0.05 = 0.027
Wood: (8.08/20.93) × 0.12 = 0.046
Metal: (1.26/20.93) × 50.0 = 3.01
Glass: (0.13/20.93) × 1.0 = 0.0062
Other: (0.20/20.93) × 0.30 = 0.0029

k_composite ≈ 0.027 + 0.046 + 3.01 + 0.0062 + 0.0029
           ≈ 3.09 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 3.06 ratio = 20.93 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 3.06 m²/m²
Density = 855 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 20.93 / (3.06 × 855)
      = 20.93 / 2616.3
      = 0.00800 m = 8.0 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 855 × 1384
    = 1,183,320 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Exhibit booths (aluminum/fabric): 1.40 kg/m² (23.9%)
- Display tables (plastic/metal): 2.67 kg/m² (45.6%)
- Registration desks (laminate): 0.080 kg/m² (1.4%)
- Chairs (metal/fabric): 0.60 kg/m² (10.2%)
- Portable partitions (foam core): 0.15 kg/m² (2.6%)
- A/V equipment (electronics): 0.12 kg/m² (2.0%)
- Signage/banners (vinyl/fabric): 0.040 kg/m² (0.7%)
- Lounge furniture (wood/fabric): 0.24 kg/m² (4.1%)
- Product displays (metal/acrylic): 0.45 kg/m² (7.7%)
- Electrical drops (plastic/copper): 0.060 kg/m² (1.0%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.048 kg/m² (0.8%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.0090 kg/m² (0.2%)
- **Total: 5.86 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Metal (aluminum/steel): 1.40 × 0.43 + 2.67 × 0.18 + 0.60 × 0.67 + 0.45 × 0.60 + 0.060 × 0.30 + 0.048 + 0.0090 = 1.82 kg/m² (31.1%)
- Plastic/Laminate: 2.67 × 0.82 + 0.080 + 0.15 + 0.12 × 0.40 + 0.060 × 0.50 = 2.46 kg/m² (42.0%)
- Fabric/Textile: 1.40 × 0.23 + 0.60 × 0.33 + 0.040 + 0.24 × 0.40 = 0.62 kg/m² (10.6%)
- Wood: 0.24 × 0.40 = 0.10 kg/m² (1.7%)
- Electronics: 0.12 × 0.60 = 0.072 kg/m² (1.2%)
- Acrylic: 0.45 × 0.40 = 0.18 kg/m² (3.1%)
- Other: 0.60 kg/m² (10.2%)

**Simplified:**
- Plastic/Laminate: 2.46 kg/m² (42.0%)
- Metal: 1.82 kg/m² (31.1%)
- Fabric/Textile: 0.62 kg/m² (10.6%)
- Acrylic/Other: 0.96 kg/m² (16.4%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Plastic/Laminate: 2.46 × 950 = 2,337
Metal: 1.82 × 3500 = 6,370
Fabric/Textile: 0.62 × 550 = 341
Acrylic/Other: 0.96 × 1300 = 1,248

ρ_composite = (2,337 + 6,370 + 341 + 1,248) / 5.86
           = 10,296 / 5.86
           = 1,757 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Plastic/Laminate: 2.46 × 1400 = 3,444
Metal: 1.82 × 480 = 874
Fabric/Textile: 0.62 × 1340 = 831
Acrylic/Other: 0.96 × 1300 = 1,248

c_p,composite = (3,444 + 874 + 831 + 1,248) / 5.86
             = 6,397 / 5.86
             = 1,092 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Plastic/Laminate: (2.46/5.86) × 0.20 = 0.084
Metal: (1.82/5.86) × 25.0 = 7.76
Fabric/Textile: (0.62/5.86) × 0.05 = 0.0053
Acrylic/Other: (0.96/5.86) × 0.30 = 0.049

k_composite ≈ 0.084 + 7.76 + 0.0053 + 0.049
           ≈ 7.90 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.00 ratio = 5.86 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.00 m²/m²
Density = 1757 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 5.86 / (2.00 × 1757)
      = 5.86 / 3514
      = 0.00167 m = 1.7 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 1757 × 1092
    = 1,918,644 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Low Surface Area, Very Low Mass - Temporary Installations:**
- Moderate density (1,757 kg/m³) - lightweight materials
- Low surface area ratio (2.00 m²/m²) - open floor plan
- High specific heat (1,092 J/kg·K) - plastic/fabric mix
- Moderate thermal conductivity (7.90 W/m-K) - metal influence
- Very low thermal mass: 5.86 kg/m² (lowest of all space types calculated)

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Very low thermal storage capacity
- Fast thermal response
- Limited temperature damping
- Lightweight, temporary character
- Large volume space

**Exhibit Hall Features:**
- **Display tables dominate** - 2.67 kg/m² (46% of mass)
- **Plastic/laminate** - 42% by mass (tables, partitions, displays)
- **Metal** - 31% by mass (frames, chairs, displays)
- **Temporary installations** - exhibit booths, partitions
- **Very low mass per floor area** - open space with sparse furnishings
- **Modular/reconfigurable** - changes per event
- **Large scale** - 200 booths, 300 tables, 500 chairs

**Convention Center Characteristics:**

- Very high peak occupancy (thousands)
- Setup/teardown periods

- Loading dock access for setup
- High ceilings (4-8m)

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Highly variable occupancy (0 during setup to 5000+ during events)
- Event-based operation (days to weeks per event)
- Very large volume to condition (high bay)

- Event-based schedule (not daily)
- Setup periods (1-3 days, doors open, loading)

- Teardown periods (1 day, doors open)
- Vacant between events

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Twin beds (metal/foam): 4.00 kg/m² (15.6%)
- Desks (laminate/wood/books): 4.00 kg/m² (15.6%)
- Desk chairs (metal/fabric): 0.90 kg/m² (3.5%)
- Dressers (particleboard/clothing): 5.00 kg/m² (19.6%)
- Bookshelves (wood/laminate/books): 3.00 kg/m² (11.7%)
- Closet storage (fabric/metal/clothing): 2.25 kg/m² (8.8%)
- Refrigerator (metal/plastic): 1.25 kg/m² (4.9%)
- Microwave (metal/plastic): 0.60 kg/m² (2.3%)
- Electronics (plastic/metal): 0.50 kg/m² (2.0%)
- Trash/recycling (plastic): 0.20 kg/m² (0.8%)
- Area rug (textile): 3.60 kg/m² (14.1%)
- Desk lamps (metal/plastic): 0.10 kg/m² (0.4%)
- Ceiling fixture (aluminum): 0.060 kg/m² (0.2%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.045 kg/m² (0.2%)
- **Total: 25.56 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Clothing/Textiles: 4.00 × 0.13 + 0.90 × 0.33 + 5.00 × 0.40 + 2.25 × 0.89 + 3.60 = 8.82 kg/m² (34.5%)
- Particleboard/Laminate: 4.00 × 0.63 + 5.00 × 0.60 + 3.00 × 0.40 = 6.72 kg/m² (26.3%)
- Books/Paper: 4.00 × 0.38 + 3.00 × 0.60 = 3.32 kg/m² (13.0%)
- Foam: 4.00 × 0.50 = 2.00 kg/m² (7.8%)
- Metal: 4.00 × 0.38 + 0.90 × 0.67 + 2.25 × 0.11 + 1.25 × 0.60 + 0.60 × 0.50 + 0.50 × 0.40 + 0.10 × 0.50 + 0.060 + 0.045 = 3.76 kg/m² (14.7%)
- Plastic: 1.25 × 0.40 + 0.60 × 0.50 + 0.50 × 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.10 × 0.50 = 1.35 kg/m² (5.3%)

**Simplified:**
- Clothing/Textiles: 8.82 kg/m² (34.5%)
- Particleboard/Laminate: 6.72 kg/m² (26.3%)
- Metal: 3.76 kg/m² (14.7%)
- Books/Paper: 3.32 kg/m² (13.0%)
- Foam: 2.00 kg/m² (7.8%)
- Plastic: 1.35 kg/m² (5.3%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Clothing/Textiles: 8.82 × 550 = 4,851
Particleboard/Laminate: 6.72 × 720 = 4,838
Metal: 3.76 × 5000 = 18,800
Books/Paper: 3.32 × 700 = 2,324
Foam: 2.00 × 30 = 60
Plastic: 1.35 × 1100 = 1,485

ρ_composite = (4,851 + 4,838 + 18,800 + 2,324 + 60 + 1,485) / 25.56
           = 32,358 / 25.56
           = 1,266 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Clothing/Textiles: 8.82 × 1340 = 11,819
Particleboard/Laminate: 6.72 × 1300 = 8,736
Metal: 3.76 × 480 = 1,805
Books/Paper: 3.32 × 1340 = 4,449
Foam: 2.00 × 1700 = 3,400
Plastic: 1.35 × 1400 = 1,890

c_p,composite = (11,819 + 8,736 + 1,805 + 4,449 + 3,400 + 1,890) / 25.56
             = 32,099 / 25.56
             = 1,256 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Clothing/Textiles: (8.82/25.56) × 0.05 = 0.017
Particleboard/Laminate: (6.72/25.56) × 0.17 = 0.045
Metal: (3.76/25.56) × 45.0 = 6.62
Books/Paper: (3.32/25.56) × 0.06 = 0.0078
Foam: (2.00/25.56) × 0.03 = 0.0023
Plastic: (1.35/25.56) × 0.20 = 0.011

k_composite ≈ 0.017 + 0.045 + 6.62 + 0.0078 + 0.0023 + 0.011
           ≈ 6.70 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 4.15 ratio = 25.56 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 4.15 m²/m²
Density = 1266 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 25.56 / (4.15 × 1266)
      = 25.56 / 5253.9
      = 0.00487 m = 4.9 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 1266 × 1256
    = 1,590,096 J/m³·K
```

- **Dressers dominate** - 5.00 kg/m² (20% of mass)

**Student Housing Characteristics:**
- 24/7 occupancy during academic year
- Seasonal vacancy (summer, breaks)
- High occupant density (2 people in 20 m²)
- Mixed use (sleeping, studying, socializing)
- Personal temperature control limited
- Variable internal gains (computers, lights)
- Privacy challenges
- Budget-conscious design

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Continuous occupancy during school year (24/7)
- 2 occupants in small space (high heat gain per area)
- Equipment heat gains (2 laptops, refrigerator, microwave)
- Lighting loads (desk lamps, overhead)
- Metabolic heat gains significant
- Ventilation critical (odor control, air quality)
- Temperature control (individual preferences vary)
- Seasonal vacancy (summer, breaks - setback)

**Operational Patterns:**
- Academic year occupancy (9 months typical)
- Summer vacancy or low occupancy
- Peak internal gains: evening (both students present)
- Variable schedule (class times differ)
- Weekend patterns different (more occupancy)
- Break periods (unoccupied)
- All-night occupancy (sleeping)
- Intermittent cooking (microwave)

**Special Considerations:**
- Occupant comfort in small space
- Noise and privacy (shared room)
- Individual temperature preferences
- Moisture control (showering elsewhere)
- Fire safety (sprinklers, smoke detectors)
- Emergency egress (window requirements)
- Electrical safety (multiple devices)
- Space efficiency maximization
- Student budget constraints
- Seasonal transitions (move-in/move-out)

k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (5.18/11.91) × 45.0 = 19.57
Foam: (2.15/11.91) × 0.03 = 0.0054
Clothing/Gear: (2.12/11.91) × 0.05 = 0.0089
Fabric: (0.72/11.91) × 0.05 = 0.0030
Laminate/Wood: (0.69/11.91) × 0.17 = 0.0098
Other: (1.05/11.91) × 100.0 = 8.82

k_composite ≈ 19.57 + 0.0054 + 0.0089 + 0.0030 + 0.0098 + 8.82
           ≈ 28.4 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.03 ratio = 11.91 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.03 m²/m²
Density = 3803 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 11.91 / (2.03 × 3803)
      = 11.91 / 7720.09
      = 0.00154 m = 1.5 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 3803 × 996
    = 3,787,788 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Treadmills (steel/electronics): 4.67 kg/m² (16.4%)
- Stationary bikes (steel): 1.87 kg/m² (6.6%)
- Ellipticals (steel): 2.67 kg/m² (9.4%)
- Weight machines (steel/iron): 7.40 kg/m² (26.0%)
- Free weight racks (steel/iron): 7.73 kg/m² (27.1%)
- Exercise benches (steel/vinyl): 0.83 kg/m² (2.9%)
- Squat racks (steel): 1.00 kg/m² (3.5%)
- Wall mirrors (glass): 0.80 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Exercise mats (foam): 0.14 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Storage shelves (steel/contents): 0.93 kg/m² (3.3%)
- Fans (metal/plastic): 0.16 kg/m² (0.6%)
- Sound system (electronics): 0.10 kg/m² (0.4%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.15 kg/m² (0.5%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.030 kg/m² (0.1%)
- **Total: 28.51 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel: 4.67 × 0.57 + 1.87 + 2.67 + 7.40 × 0.32 + 7.73 × 0.14 + 0.83 × 0.80 + 1.00 + 0.93 × 0.57 + 0.16 × 0.60 + 0.15 + 0.030 = 12.81 kg/m² (44.9%)
- Iron (weights): 7.40 × 0.54 + 7.73 × 0.86 = 10.64 kg/m² (37.3%)
- Electronics: 4.67 × 0.29 + 0.10 = 1.45 kg/m² (5.1%)
- Rubber/Plastic: 4.67 × 0.14 + 0.83 × 0.20 + 0.93 × 0.43 + 0.16 × 0.40 = 1.50 kg/m² (5.3%)
- Glass: 0.80 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Foam: 0.14 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Other: 1.17 kg/m² (4.1%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 12.81 kg/m² (44.9%)
- Iron (weights): 10.64 kg/m² (37.3%)
- Rubber/Plastic: 1.50 kg/m² (5.3%)
- Electronics: 1.45 kg/m² (5.1%)
- Glass: 0.80 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Other: 1.31 kg/m² (4.6%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 12.81 × 7850 = 100,559
Iron: 10.64 × 7870 = 83,737
Rubber/Plastic: 1.50 × 1100 = 1,650
Electronics: 1.45 × 2500 = 3,625
Glass: 0.80 × 2500 = 2,000
Other: 1.31 × 1200 = 1,572

ρ_composite = (100,559 + 83,737 + 1,650 + 3,625 + 2,000 + 1,572) / 28.51
           = 193,143 / 28.51
           = 6,774 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 12.81 × 460 = 5,893
Iron: 10.64 × 460 = 4,894
Rubber/Plastic: 1.50 × 1400 = 2,100
Electronics: 1.45 × 800 = 1,160
Glass: 0.80 × 840 = 672
Other: 1.31 × 1200 = 1,572

c_p,composite = (5,893 + 4,894 + 2,100 + 1,160 + 672 + 1,572) / 28.51
             = 16,291 / 28.51
             = 571 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (12.81/28.51) × 45.0 = 20.22
Iron: (10.64/28.51) × 80.0 = 29.85
Rubber/Plastic: (1.50/28.51) × 0.20 = 0.011
Electronics: (1.45/28.51) × 1.5 = 0.076
Glass: (0.80/28.51) × 1.0 = 0.028
Other: (1.31/28.51) × 0.50 = 0.023

k_composite ≈ 20.22 + 29.85 + 0.011 + 0.076 + 0.028 + 0.023
           ≈ 50.2 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 1.79 ratio = 28.51 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 1.79 m²/m²
Density = 6774 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 28.51 / (1.79 × 6774)
      = 28.51 / 12125.46
      = 0.00235 m = 2.4 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 6774 × 571
    = 3,868,154 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Basketball goals (steel/acrylic): 0.50 kg/m² (12.8%)
- Volleyball nets (steel/nylon): 0.11 kg/m² (2.8%)
- Scoreboards (electronics): 0.20 kg/m² (5.1%)
- Bleachers (steel): 2.00 kg/m² (51.2%)
- Wall padding (vinyl/foam): 0.38 kg/m² (9.7%)
- Storage carts (steel): 0.25 kg/m² (6.4%)
- Folding chairs (steel): 0.10 kg/m² (2.6%)
- Shot clocks (electronics): 0.025 kg/m² (0.6%)
- Sound system (electronics): 0.075 kg/m² (1.9%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.20 kg/m² (5.1%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.038 kg/m² (1.0%)
- **Total: 3.91 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel: 0.50 × 0.75 + 0.11 × 0.89 + 2.00 + 0.25 + 0.10 = 2.82 kg/m² (72.1%)
- Acrylic/Plastic: 0.50 × 0.25 + 0.38 × 0.30 = 0.24 kg/m² (6.1%)
- Foam: 0.38 × 0.70 = 0.27 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Aluminum: 0.20 + 0.038 = 0.24 kg/m² (6.1%)
- Electronics: 0.20 + 0.025 + 0.075 = 0.30 kg/m² (7.7%)
- Nylon: 0.11 × 0.11 = 0.012 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Other: 0.03 kg/m² (0.8%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 2.82 kg/m² (72.1%)
- Electronics: 0.30 kg/m² (7.7%)
- Foam: 0.27 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Acrylic/Plastic: 0.24 kg/m² (6.1%)
- Aluminum: 0.24 kg/m² (6.1%)
- Other: 0.04 kg/m² (1.0%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 2.82 × 7850 = 22,137
Electronics: 0.30 × 2500 = 750
Foam: 0.27 × 50 = 14
Acrylic/Plastic: 0.24 × 1200 = 288
Aluminum: 0.24 × 2700 = 648
Other: 0.04 × 1000 = 40

ρ_composite = (22,137 + 750 + 14 + 288 + 648 + 40) / 3.91
           = 23,877 / 3.91
           = 6,107 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 2.82 × 460 = 1,297
Electronics: 0.30 × 800 = 240
Foam: 0.27 × 1700 = 459
Acrylic/Plastic: 0.24 × 1400 = 336
Aluminum: 0.24 × 900 = 216
Other: 0.04 × 1000 = 40

c_p,composite = (1,297 + 240 + 459 + 336 + 216 + 40) / 3.91
             = 2,588 / 3.91
             = 662 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (2.82/3.91) × 45.0 = 32.45
Electronics: (0.30/3.91) × 1.5 = 0.12
Foam: (0.27/3.91) × 0.04 = 0.0028
Acrylic/Plastic: (0.24/3.91) × 0.20 = 0.012
Aluminum: (0.24/3.91) × 205.0 = 12.58
Other: (0.04/3.91) × 0.50 = 0.0051

k_composite ≈ 32.45 + 0.12 + 0.0028 + 0.012 + 12.58 + 0.0051
           ≈ 45.2 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 0.50 ratio = 3.91 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 0.50 m²/m²
Density = 6107 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 3.91 / (0.50 × 6107)
      = 3.91 / 3053.5
      = 0.00128 m = 1.3 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 6107 × 662
    = 4,042,834 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Very Low Surface Area, Very Low Mass - Open Court:**
- High density (6,107 kg/m³) - steel dominated (72%)
- Very low surface area ratio (0.50 m²/m²) - minimal equipment
- Low specific heat (662 J/kg·K) - metallic character
- Very high thermal conductivity (45.2 W/m-K) - steel/aluminum
- Very low thermal mass: 3.91 kg/m² (second lowest after exhibit space)

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Very low thermal storage capacity
- Fast thermal response
- Minimal temperature damping
- Large open volume space
- Dominated by envelope and HVAC

### Design Appropriateness

**Playing Area Features:**
- **Bleachers dominate** - 2.00 kg/m² (51% of mass)
- **Steel construction** - 72% by mass (bleachers, goals, carts, chairs)
- **Very sparse furnishings** - mostly open floor
- **Multi-sport capability** - basketball, volleyball, indoor soccer
- **Large volume** - high ceilings (6-12 m) for ball clearance
- **Minimal internal mass** - thermal behavior dominated by envelope
- **Spectator seating** - retractable bleachers (200 seats)
- **Safety features** - wall padding, court markings

**Gymnasium Characteristics:**
- Large open floor plan (500-1,500 m²)
- Very high ceilings (6-12 m)
- Multi-purpose use (sports, events, assemblies)
- Variable occupancy (10-200+ people)
- Event-based peak use (games, tournaments)
- Physical education during school hours
- Community use evenings/weekends
- Spectator events (games, performances)

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Very large volume to condition (high bay)
- Variable occupancy (10 to 200+ people)
- High metabolic heat gains during events (playing + spectators)
- Stratification challenges (high ceiling, warm air rises)
- Destratification fans often needed
- Pre-conditioning for events
- Setback during unoccupied periods
- Intermittent high loads

**Operational Patterns:**
- School hours: Physical education classes
- After school: Practice, team sports (3-6pm)
- Evenings: Games, events, community use (6-10pm)
- Weekends: Tournaments, rentals, community events
- Summer: Camps, reduced use, or closed
- Variable schedule (event-dependent)
- Peak occupancy: Games and tournaments
- Low occupancy: Practice sessions

**Special Considerations:**
- Very high metabolic gains during games (200+ people active/spectating)
- Large volume heating/cooling challenge
- Thermal stratification (6-12 m ceiling height)
- Destratification required (ceiling fans)
- Acoustics (sound reflection, echoes)
- Lighting levels (competition vs. practice)
- Emergency egress (large crowds)
- Floor protection (hardwood maintenance)
- Equipment storage (nets, goals, carts)
- Spectator comfort (bleachers, temperature)

- Foam: 2.83 × 0.35 = 0.99 kg/m² (11.8%)

- Plastic: 0.70 × 0.00 + 0.067 + 0.050 = 0.12 kg/m² (1.4%)
- Aluminum: 0.20 + 0.036 = 0.24 kg/m² (2.9%)

- Electronics: 0.96 kg/m² (11.5%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 3.46 × 7850 = 27,161
Electronics: 0.96 × 2500 = 2,400
Foam: 0.99 × 30 = 30
Medical Supplies: 0.93 × 1200 = 1,116
Fabric: 0.51 × 550 = 281
Vinyl: 0.32 × 1300 = 416
Aluminum: 0.24 × 2700 = 648
Other: 0.95 × 1500 = 1,425

ρ_composite = (27,161 + 2,400 + 30 + 1,116 + 281 + 416 + 648 + 1,425) / 8.36
           = 33,477 / 8.36
           = 4,004 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 3.46 × 460 = 1,592
Electronics: 0.96 × 800 = 768
Foam: 0.99 × 1700 = 1,683
Medical Supplies: 0.93 × 1300 = 1,209
Fabric: 0.51 × 1340 = 683
Vinyl: 0.32 × 1400 = 448
Aluminum: 0.24 × 900 = 216
Other: 0.95 × 1100 = 1,045

c_p,composite = (1,592 + 768 + 1,683 + 1,209 + 683 + 448 + 216 + 1,045) / 8.36
             = 7,644 / 8.36
             = 914 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (3.46/8.36) × 45.0 = 18.63
Electronics: (0.96/8.36) × 1.5 = 0.17
Foam: (0.99/8.36) × 0.03 = 0.0036
Medical Supplies: (0.93/8.36) × 0.30 = 0.033
Fabric: (0.51/8.36) × 0.05 = 0.0030
Vinyl: (0.32/8.36) × 0.19 = 0.0073
Aluminum: (0.24/8.36) × 205.0 = 5.89
Other: (0.95/8.36) × 0.80 = 0.091

k_composite ≈ 18.63 + 0.17 + 0.0036 + 0.033 + 0.0030 + 0.0073 + 5.89 + 0.091
           ≈ 24.8 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 1.89 ratio = 8.36 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 1.89 m²/m²
Density = 4004 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 8.36 / (1.89 × 4004)
      = 8.36 / 7567.56
      = 0.00110 m = 1.1 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 4004 × 914
    = 3,659,656 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Low Surface Area, Low Mass - Medical Equipment:**
- High density (4,004 kg/m³) - steel dominated (41%)
- Low surface area ratio (1.89 m²/m²) - compact medical equipment
- Low specific heat (914 J/kg·K) - metallic character
- Very high thermal conductivity (24.8 W/m-K) - steel/aluminum
- Low thermal mass: 8.36 kg/m²

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Low thermal storage capacity
- Fast thermal response
- Limited temperature damping
- Medical equipment dominated
- Critical care environment

### Design Appropriateness

**Emergency Room Features:**
- **Hospital beds dominate** - 2.83 kg/m² (34% of mass)
- **Steel construction** - 41% by mass (beds, carts, cabinets, stools)
- **Privacy curtains** - 0.696 m²/m² surface area (37% of total)
- **Medical equipment** - monitors, crash carts, IV pumps
- **10 treatment bays** - beds, monitors, IV poles
- **Emergency capability** - 2 crash carts with defibrillators
- **Infection control** - antimicrobial curtains, hand sanitizers
- **24/7 operation** - continuous emergency coverage

**Healthcare Emergency Characteristics:**
- 24/7 operation year-round
- High-acuity patient care
- Variable occupancy (highly unpredictable)
- Trauma and emergency treatment
- Rapid patient turnover
- Critical care equipment
- Infection control protocols
- HIPAA privacy requirements

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- 24/7 operation (no setback periods)
- High ventilation requirements (infection control)
- Positive pressure relative to corridors
- Minimum 6 air changes per hour
- HEPA filtration in some areas
- Temperature control critical (patient comfort)
- Equipment heat gains (monitors, computers, lights)
- Variable occupancy (unpredictable)

**Operational Patterns:**
- Continuous 24/7/365 operation
- No predictable occupancy pattern
- Peak periods often late evening/night
- Equipment runs continuously (monitors, computers)
- High internal gains from medical equipment
- Lighting always on (emergency readiness)
- No energy recovery opportunities
- Critical backup power required

**Special Considerations:**
- Infection control (air pressure, filtration, ACH)
- Temperature stability (patient care quality)
- Humidity control (patient comfort, infection)
- Critical backup power (life safety)
- Medical gas systems (oxygen, suction, air)
- Noise control (patient healing environment)
- HIPAA compliance (privacy curtains, spacing)
- Equipment heat gains (monitors, computers)
- Emergency lighting and power
- Redundant HVAC systems (reliability)

             = 9,382 / 10.40
             = 902 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (5.44/10.40) × 45.0 = 23.54
Laminate/Wood: (1.67/10.40) × 0.17 = 0.027
Medical Supplies: (1.01/10.40) × 0.30 = 0.029
Vinyl/Padding: (0.74/10.40) × 0.19 = 0.014
Electronics: (0.67/10.40) × 1.5 = 0.097
Plastic: (0.69/10.40) × 0.20 = 0.013
Aluminum: (0.33/10.40) × 205.0 = 6.51
Other: (0.51/10.40) × 0.50 = 0.025

k_composite ≈ 23.54 + 0.027 + 0.029 + 0.014 + 0.097 + 0.013 + 6.51 + 0.025
           ≈ 30.3 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.30 ratio = 10.40 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.30 m²/m²
Density = 4812 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 10.40 / (2.30 × 4812)
      = 10.40 / 11067.6
      = 0.00094 m = 0.9 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 4812 × 902
    = 4,340,424 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Medical shelving (steel/supplies): 22.00 kg/m² (47.9%)
- Medication cabinet (steel/glass): 3.65 kg/m² (7.9%)
- Linen shelving (steel/textile): 7.00 kg/m² (15.2%)
- Supply carts (steel): 4.50 kg/m² (9.8%)
- Storage cabinet (steel): 3.25 kg/m² (7.1%)
- Refrigerator (steel): 4.75 kg/m² (10.3%)
- Step stool (steel): 0.25 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Inventory scanner (electronics): 0.15 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Waste bin (plastic): 0.10 kg/m² (0.2%)
- Hand sanitizer (plastic): 0.050 kg/m² (0.1%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.20 kg/m² (0.4%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.045 kg/m² (0.1%)
- **Total: 45.94 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel: 22.00 × 0.32 + 3.65 × 0.62 + 7.00 × 0.43 + 4.50 + 3.25 + 4.75 + 0.25 = 23.56 kg/m² (51.3%)
- Medical Supplies: 22.00 × 0.68 + 3.65 × 0.27 = 15.95 kg/m² (34.7%)
- Linens/Textile: 7.00 × 0.57 = 3.99 kg/m² (8.7%)
- Glass: 3.65 × 0.11 = 0.40 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Aluminum: 0.20 + 0.045 = 0.25 kg/m² (0.5%)
- Plastic: 0.10 + 0.050 = 0.15 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Electronics: 0.15 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Other: 1.49 kg/m² (3.2%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 23.56 kg/m² (51.3%)
- Medical Supplies: 15.95 kg/m² (34.7%)
- Linens/Textile: 3.99 kg/m² (8.7%)
- Glass: 0.40 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Other: 2.04 kg/m² (4.4%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 23.56 × 7850 = 184,946
Medical Supplies: 15.95 × 1200 = 19,140
Linens/Textile: 3.99 × 550 = 2,195
Glass: 0.40 × 2500 = 1,000
Other: 2.04 × 2000 = 4,080

ρ_composite = (184,946 + 19,140 + 2,195 + 1,000 + 4,080) / 45.94
           = 211,361 / 45.94
           = 4,600 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 23.56 × 460 = 10,838
Medical Supplies: 15.95 × 1300 = 20,735
Linens/Textile: 3.99 × 1340 = 5,347
Glass: 0.40 × 840 = 336
Other: 2.04 × 1100 = 2,244

c_p,composite = (10,838 + 20,735 + 5,347 + 336 + 2,244) / 45.94
             = 39,500 / 45.94
             = 860 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (23.56/45.94) × 45.0 = 23.08
Medical Supplies: (15.95/45.94) × 0.30 = 0.10
Linens/Textile: (3.99/45.94) × 0.05 = 0.0043
Glass: (0.40/45.94) × 1.0 = 0.0087
Other: (2.04/45.94) × 150.0 = 6.67

k_composite ≈ 23.08 + 0.10 + 0.0043 + 0.0087 + 6.67
           ≈ 29.9 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 5.95 ratio = 45.94 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 5.95 m²/m²
Density = 4600 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 45.94 / (5.95 × 4600)
      = 45.94 / 27370
      = 0.00168 m = 1.7 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 4600 × 860
    = 3,956,000 J/m³·K
```

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Bassinets (acrylic/metal): 2.50 kg/m² (21.6%)
- Infant warmers (steel): 1.13 kg/m² (9.7%)
- Patient monitors (electronics): 0.63 kg/m² (5.4%)
- Supply carts (steel/plastic): 1.31 kg/m² (11.3%)
- Nursing counter (laminate): 1.00 kg/m² (8.6%)
- Rocking chairs (wood/fabric): 1.15 kg/m² (9.9%)
- Phototherapy (metal/plastic): 0.63 kg/m² (5.4%)
- Storage cabinets (steel/glass): 1.25 kg/m² (10.8%)
- Sinks (steel): 0.38 kg/m² (3.3%)
- Resuscitation cart (steel): 0.88 kg/m² (7.6%)
- Medical gas (brass/steel): 0.30 kg/m² (2.6%)
- Waste bins (plastic): 0.094 kg/m² (0.8%)
- Hand sanitizers (plastic): 0.075 kg/m² (0.6%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.25 kg/m² (2.2%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.045 kg/m² (0.4%)
- **Total: 11.60 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Steel: 2.50 × 0.48 + 1.13 + 1.31 × 0.43 + 1.25 × 0.60 + 0.38 + 0.88 + 0.30 × 0.70 = 4.68 kg/m² (40.3%)
- Acrylic: 2.50 × 0.32 = 0.80 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Wood: 1.15 × 0.65 = 0.75 kg/m² (6.5%)
- Laminate: 1.00 × 0.75 = 0.75 kg/m² (6.5%)
- Fabric/Padding: 2.50 × 0.12 + 1.15 × 0.35 = 0.70 kg/m² (6.0%)
- Medical Supplies: 1.31 × 0.57 + 1.25 × 0.40 = 1.25 kg/m² (10.8%)
- Electronics: 0.63 + 1.00 × 0.25 = 0.88 kg/m² (7.6%)
- Plastic: 0.63 × 0.40 + 0.094 + 0.075 = 0.42 kg/m² (3.6%)
- Aluminum: 0.25 + 0.045 = 0.30 kg/m² (2.6%)
- Other: 1.07 kg/m² (9.2%)

**Simplified:**
- Steel: 4.68 kg/m² (40.3%)
- Medical Supplies: 1.25 kg/m² (10.8%)
- Electronics: 0.88 kg/m² (7.6%)
- Acrylic: 0.80 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Wood: 0.75 kg/m² (6.5%)
- Laminate: 0.75 kg/m² (6.5%)
- Fabric/Padding: 0.70 kg/m² (6.0%)
- Other: 1.79 kg/m² (15.4%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 4.68 × 7850 = 36,738
Medical Supplies: 1.25 × 1200 = 1,500
Electronics: 0.88 × 2500 = 2,200
Acrylic: 0.80 × 1200 = 960
Wood: 0.75 × 600 = 450
Laminate: 0.75 × 720 = 540
Fabric/Padding: 0.70 × 550 = 385
Other: 1.79 × 2000 = 3,580

ρ_composite = (36,738 + 1,500 + 2,200 + 960 + 450 + 540 + 385 + 3,580) / 11.60
           = 46,353 / 11.60
           = 3,996 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 4.68 × 460 = 2,153
Medical Supplies: 1.25 × 1300 = 1,625
Electronics: 0.88 × 800 = 704
Acrylic: 0.80 × 1400 = 1,120
Wood: 0.75 × 1600 = 1,200
Laminate: 0.75 × 1300 = 975
Fabric/Padding: 0.70 × 1340 = 938
Other: 1.79 × 1100 = 1,969

c_p,composite = (2,153 + 1,625 + 704 + 1,120 + 1,200 + 975 + 938 + 1,969) / 11.60
             = 10,684 / 11.60
             = 921 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (4.68/11.60) × 45.0 = 18.16
Medical Supplies: (1.25/11.60) × 0.30 = 0.032
Electronics: (0.88/11.60) × 1.5 = 0.11
Acrylic: (0.80/11.60) × 0.19 = 0.013
Wood: (0.75/11.60) × 0.12 = 0.0078
Laminate: (0.75/11.60) × 0.17 = 0.011
Fabric/Padding: (0.70/11.60) × 0.05 = 0.0030
Other: (1.79/11.60) × 150.0 = 23.2

k_composite ≈ 18.16 + 0.032 + 0.11 + 0.013 + 0.0078 + 0.011 + 0.0030 + 23.2
           ≈ 41.5 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.48 ratio = 11.60 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.48 m²/m²
Density = 3996 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 11.60 / (2.48 × 3996)
      = 11.60 / 9910.08
      = 0.00117 m = 1.2 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 3996 × 921
    = 3,680,316 J/m³·K
```

## Key Observations

### Thermal Mass Characteristics

**Moderate Surface Area, Low Mass - Specialized Neonatal Care:**
- High density (3,996 kg/m³) - steel dominated (40%)
- Moderate surface area ratio (2.48 m²/m²) - bassinets and equipment
- Low specific heat (921 J/kg·K) - metallic/acrylic character
- Very high thermal conductivity (41.5 W/m-K) - steel/aluminum/warmers
- Low thermal mass: 11.60 kg/m²

**Thermal Behavior:**
- Low thermal storage capacity
- Fast thermal response
- Limited temperature damping
- Medical equipment and bassinet dominated
- Critical temperature control environment

### Design Appropriateness

**Hospital Nursery Features:**
- **Bassinets dominate** - 2.50 kg/m² (22% of mass)
- **Steel construction** - 40% by mass (warmers, carts, cabinets, sinks)
- **8 bassinets** - newborn care capacity
- **2 infant warmers** - temperature regulation for unstable infants
- **10 patient monitors** - continuous vital signs monitoring
- **Rocking chairs** - feeding and bonding
- **Phototherapy units** - jaundice treatment
- **Resuscitation cart** - emergency neonatal care

**Healthcare Nursery Characteristics:**
- 24/7 operation year-round
- Critical temperature control (24-26°C)
- Strict infection control protocols
- Family visitation and bonding
- Continuous patient monitoring
- Neonatal care expertise
- Emergency resuscitation capability
- Breastfeeding support

### Modeling Implications

**HVAC Considerations:**
- 24/7/365 operation (no setback periods)
- Critical temperature stability (24-26°C)
- Narrow temperature tolerance (±1°C)
- High ventilation requirements (minimum 6 ACH)
- HEPA filtration (infection control)
- Positive pressure relative to corridors
- Equipment heat gains (warmers, phototherapy, monitors)
- Infant warmer heat output significant
- No temperature setback allowed

**Operational Patterns:**
- Continuous 24/7/365 operation
- Variable census (6-10 newborns typical)
- Infant warmers intermittent use (high heat output)
- Phototherapy continuous when in use
- Peak staffing: day shift (more procedures)
- Night operations: reduced activity but full monitoring
- Equipment runs continuously
- Critical backup power required

**Special Considerations:**
- Critical temperature stability (newborn thermoregulation)
- Humidity control (40-60% RH for infant comfort)
- Infection control (air pressure, filtration, ACH)
- Noise control (infant sleep and development)
- Lighting levels (day/night cycles for circadian rhythm)
- Equipment heat gains (infant warmers 200-300W each)
- Emergency backup power (life safety systems)
- Family comfort (chairs, bonding areas)
- Resuscitation readiness
- Strict hand hygiene compliance

## Material Property Calculations

### Mass-Weighted Composite Properties

**Component Mass Breakdown:**
- Charting counter (laminate): 3.67 kg/m² (18.9%)
- Computers (electronics): 2.00 kg/m² (10.3%)
- Supply cabinets (steel/laminate): 6.00 kg/m² (30.9%)
- Med prep counter (laminate): 1.50 kg/m² (7.7%)
- Office chairs (steel/fabric): 2.00 kg/m² (10.3%)
- Monitor screens (electronics): 0.80 kg/m² (4.1%)
- Chart rack (steel): 1.33 kg/m² (6.9%)
- Printer/fax (electronics): 0.83 kg/m² (4.3%)
- Pneumatic tube (plastic/metal): 0.27 kg/m² (1.4%)
- Communications (electronics): 0.17 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Waste bins (plastic): 0.17 kg/m² (0.9%)
- Hand sanitizers (plastic): 0.067 kg/m² (0.3%)
- Sharps container (plastic): 0.067 kg/m² (0.3%)
- White board (plastic): 0.17 kg/m² (0.9%)
- LED fixtures (aluminum): 0.27 kg/m² (1.4%)
- HVAC (aluminum): 0.060 kg/m² (0.3%)
- **Total: 19.40 kg/m²**

### Material Composition

**By Mass:**
- Laminate/Wood: 3.67 × 0.73 + 6.00 × 0.42 + 1.50 × 0.67 = 6.20 kg/m² (32.0%)
- Steel: 6.00 × 0.58 + 2.00 × 0.67 + 1.33 = 6.15 kg/m² (31.7%)
- Electronics: 2.00 + 0.80 + 0.83 + 0.17 = 3.80 kg/m² (19.6%)
- Medical Supplies: 3.67 × 0.27 + 1.50 × 0.33 + 1.33 × 0.38 = 1.99 kg/m² (10.3%)
- Fabric/Padding: 2.00 × 0.33 = 0.66 kg/m² (3.4%)
- Plastic: 0.27 + 0.17 + 0.067 + 0.067 + 0.17 = 0.74 kg/m² (3.8%)
- Aluminum: 0.27 + 0.060 = 0.33 kg/m² (1.7%)

**Simplified:**
- Laminate/Wood: 6.20 kg/m² (32.0%)
- Steel: 6.15 kg/m² (31.7%)
- Electronics: 3.80 kg/m² (19.6%)
- Medical Supplies: 1.99 kg/m² (10.3%)
- Fabric/Padding: 0.66 kg/m² (3.4%)
- Other: 1.07 kg/m² (5.5%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Laminate/Wood: 6.20 × 720 = 4,464
Steel: 6.15 × 7850 = 48,278
Electronics: 3.80 × 2500 = 9,500
Medical Supplies: 1.99 × 1200 = 2,388
Fabric/Padding: 0.66 × 550 = 363
Other: 1.07 × 1500 = 1,605

ρ_composite = (4,464 + 48,278 + 9,500 + 2,388 + 363 + 1,605) / 19.40
           = 66,598 / 19.40
           = 3,433 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Laminate/Wood: 6.20 × 1300 = 8,060
Steel: 6.15 × 460 = 2,829
Electronics: 3.80 × 800 = 3,040
Medical Supplies: 1.99 × 1300 = 2,587
Fabric/Padding: 0.66 × 1340 = 884
Other: 1.07 × 1100 = 1,177

c_p,composite = (8,060 + 2,829 + 3,040 + 2,587 + 884 + 1,177) / 19.40
             = 18,577 / 19.40
             = 958 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Laminate/Wood: (6.20/19.40) × 0.17 = 0.054
Steel: (6.15/19.40) × 45.0 = 14.27
Electronics: (3.80/19.40) × 1.5 = 0.29
Medical Supplies: (1.99/19.40) × 0.30 = 0.031
Fabric/Padding: (0.66/19.40) × 0.05 = 0.0017
Other: (1.07/19.40) × 100.0 = 5.52

k_composite ≈ 0.054 + 14.27 + 0.29 + 0.031 + 0.0017 + 5.52
           ≈ 20.2 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 3.71 ratio = 19.40 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 3.71 m²/m²
Density = 3433 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 19.40 / (3.71 × 3433)
      = 19.40 / 12736.43
      = 0.00152 m = 1.5 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 3433 × 958
    = 3,288,814 J/m³·K
```

- Steel: 18.50 kg/m² (69.0%)
- Aluminum: 4.00 kg/m² (14.9%)
- Electronics: 2.00 kg/m² (7.5%)
- Medical Supplies: 1.80 kg/m² (6.7%)
- Lead: 0.47 kg/m² (1.8%)
- Other: 0.05 kg/m² (0.2%)

### Weighted Average Density

```
ρ_composite = Σ(m_i × ρ_i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 18.50 × 7850 = 145,225
Aluminum: 4.00 × 2700 = 10,800
Electronics: 2.00 × 2500 = 5,000
Medical Supplies: 1.80 × 1500 = 2,700
Lead: 0.47 × 11340 = 5,330
Other: 0.05 × 1000 = 50

ρ_composite = (145,225 + 10,800 + 5,000 + 2,700 + 5,330 + 50) / 26.82
           = 169,105 / 26.82
           = 6,305 kg/m³
```

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel: 18.50 × 460 = 8,510
Aluminum: 4.00 × 900 = 3,600
Electronics: 2.00 × 800 = 1,600
Medical Supplies: 1.80 × 1200 = 2,160
Lead: 0.47 × 130 = 61
Other: 0.05 × 1000 = 50

c_p,composite = (8,510 + 3,600 + 1,600 + 2,160 + 61 + 50) / 26.82
             = 15,981 / 26.82
             = 596 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i/V_total × k_i)

Steel: (18.50/26.82) × 45.0 = 31.04
Aluminum: (4.00/26.82) × 205.0 = 30.57
Electronics: (2.00/26.82) × 1.5 = 0.11
Medical Supplies: (1.80/26.82) × 0.30 = 0.020
Lead: (0.47/26.82) × 35.0 = 0.61
Other: (0.05/26.82) × 0.50 = 0.001

k_composite ≈ 31.04 + 30.57 + 0.11 + 0.020 + 0.61 + 0.001
           ≈ 62.4 W/m·K
```

### Effective Thickness

```
Total Mass at 2.81 ratio = 26.82 kg/m²
Surface Area Ratio = 2.81 m²/m²
Density = 6305 kg/m³

t_eff = Total Mass / (Surface Area Ratio × Density)
      = 26.82 / (2.81 × 6305)
      = 26.82 / 17717.05
      = 0.00151 m = 1.5 mm
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 6305 × 596
    = 3,757,780 J/m³·K
```

**HVAC Considerations:**
- Very high air change rates (20-25 ACH minimum)
- HEPA filtration (infection control)
- Positive pressure relative to corridors
- Critical temperature stability (18-24°C typical)
- Humidity control (30-60% RH prevents static)
- No setback when OR suite is active
- Very high equipment heat gains (surgical lights 20-40kW, C-arm, monitors)
- Surgical lights generate massive heat (compensated by high ACH)
- Laminar air flow over surgical field

**Operational Patterns:**

- Turnover time between cases (30-60 min cleaning)

**Special Considerations:**
- Critical temperature/humidity stability (surgical precision)

- Sterility maintenance (positive pressure, air quality)
- Staff comfort (cool temperatures for gowned staff)

- Emergency backup power (life safety)

## Composite Property Calculations

### Weighted Average Density

```
Volume per m² of floor:

Steel:      6.85 / 7850  = 0.000873 m³/m²
Foam:       1.30 / 50    = 0.026000 m³/m²
Fabric:     0.667 / 200  = 0.003335 m³/m²
Laminate:   0.433 / 720  = 0.000601 m³/m²
Plastic:    0.373 / 1100 = 0.000339 m³/m²

Total volume = 0.000873 + 0.026000 + 0.003335 + 0.000601 + 0.000339
             = 0.031148 m³/m²

Composite density = total mass / total volume
                  = 9.623 / 0.031148
                  = 309 kg/m³
```

> Foam (mattress + chair cushions) dominates volume at 83.5% of total, pulling the composite density below typical solid material values. This accurately reflects the physical reality of patient room furnishings, where the mattress volume is large relative to the room floor area.

### Weighted Average Specific Heat

```
c_p,composite = Σ(m_i × c_p,i) / Σ(m_i)

Steel:      6.85  × 460  = 3,151
Foam:       1.30  × 1400 = 1,820
Fabric:     0.667 × 1340 = 893
Laminate:   0.433 × 1300 = 563
Plastic:    0.373 × 1300 = 485

c_p,composite = (3,151 + 1,820 + 893 + 563 + 485) / 9.623
              = 6,912 / 9.623
              = 718 J/kg·K
```

### Weighted Average Conductivity

```
k_composite ≈ Σ(V_i / V_total × k_i)

Steel:     (0.000873 / 0.031148) × 45.0 = 0.02802 × 45.0 = 1.261
Foam:      (0.026000 / 0.031148) × 0.04 = 0.83470 × 0.04 = 0.033
Fabric:    (0.003335 / 0.031148) × 0.05 = 0.10707 × 0.05 = 0.005
Laminate:  (0.000601 / 0.031148) × 0.17 = 0.01929 × 0.17 = 0.003
Plastic:   (0.000339 / 0.031148) × 0.20 = 0.01089 × 0.20 = 0.002

k_composite ≈ 1.261 + 0.033 + 0.005 + 0.003 + 0.002
            ≈ 1.304 W/m·K
```

> Despite steel being the dominant material by mass, foam dominates the volume fraction (83.5%), which dramatically reduces the composite thermal conductivity relative to a purely steel or mixed-solid composite. This reflects the insulating quality of foam mattresses as the largest volumetric component.

### Effective Thickness

```
t_eff = Total mass per m² / (SA_ratio × composite density)
      = 9.623 / (1.224 × 309)
      = 9.623 / 378.2
      = 0.02544 m ≈ 0.025 m  (25 mm)
```

### Thermal Capacitance

```
C_v = ρ × c_p
    = 309 × 718
    = 221,862 J/m³·K
```
